import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory

The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics has the entry "Problems in loop theory and
quasigroup theory consider generalizations of groups", pointing to the article below. This file
states the open problems of that article that have a statable proposition.

Mathlib has no theory of loops, so the file introduces the needed notions: loops, subloops,
normal subloops, the centre, central nilpotency and solvability, the multiplication and inner
mapping groups, isotopy, the free Moufang loop, and laws of a loop.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Problems in loop theory and quasigroup
  theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- R. H. Bruck, *A survey of binary systems*, Springer (1958), for the standard loop-theoretic
  notions used below.
-/

namespace ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory

noncomputable section

universe u v

/-- A *loop* is a set with a binary operation `*` and a two-sided identity `1` in which
every equation `a * x = b` and `y * a = b` has a unique solution, i.e. all left and right
translations are bijections. -/
class Loop (Q : Type u) extends MulOneClass Q where
  mul_left_bijective (a : Q) : Function.Bijective (a * ·)
  mul_right_bijective (a : Q) : Function.Bijective (· * a)

namespace Loop

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

/-- The left translation `L_a : x ↦ a * x` as a permutation of the loop. -/
def leftMul (a : Q) : Equiv.Perm Q := Equiv.ofBijective _ (mul_left_bijective a)

/-- The right translation `R_a : x ↦ x * a` as a permutation of the loop. -/
def rightMul (a : Q) : Equiv.Perm Q := Equiv.ofBijective _ (mul_right_bijective a)

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma leftMul_apply (a x : Q) : leftMul a x = a * x := rfl

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma rightMul_apply (a x : Q) : rightMul a x = x * a := rfl

/-- Left division: `a ⧵ b` is the unique solution `x` of `a * x = b`. -/
def ldiv (a b : Q) : Q := (leftMul a).symm b

/-- Right division: `a / b` is the unique solution `y` of `y * b = a`. -/
instance : Div Q := ⟨fun a b => (rightMul b).symm a⟩

@[inherit_doc] scoped infixl:70 " ⧵ " => ldiv

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_ldiv (a b : Q) : a * (a ⧵ b) = b := (leftMul a).apply_symm_apply b

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma ldiv_mul (a b : Q) : a ⧵ (a * b) = b := (leftMul a).symm_apply_apply b

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma rdiv_mul (a b : Q) : a / b * b = a := (rightMul b).apply_symm_apply a

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_rdiv (a b : Q) : a * b / b = a := (rightMul b).symm_apply_apply a

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_left_cancel {a b c : Q} (h : a * b = a * c) : b = c := (mul_left_bijective a).1 h

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_right_cancel {a b c : Q} (h : b * a = c * a) : b = c := (mul_right_bijective a).1 h

/-- The left inverse `x^λ = 1 / x` of `x`, the unique element with `x^λ * x = 1`. -/
def leftInv (x : Q) : Q := 1 / x

/-- The right inverse `x^ρ = x ⧵ 1` of `x`, the unique element with `x * x^ρ = 1`. -/
def rightInv (x : Q) : Q := x ⧵ 1

/-- Powers in a loop, bracketed to the left of the last factor: `x ^ 0 = 1` and
`x ^ (n + 1) = x * x ^ n`. In a power-associative loop (e.g. any Moufang loop) this agrees with
every other bracketing. -/
instance : Pow Q ℕ := ⟨fun x n => Nat.rec 1 (fun _ y => x * y) n⟩

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma pow_zero (x : Q) : x ^ 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma pow_succ (x : Q) (n : ℕ) : x ^ (n + 1) = x * x ^ n := rfl

/-- A loop is a group if and only if it is associative. -/
def IsAssociative (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y z : Q, x * y * z = x * (y * z)

/-- A loop is commutative if `x * y = y * x` for all `x`, `y`. -/
def IsCommutative (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y : Q, x * y = y * x

/-- A loop is an abelian group if and only if it is associative and commutative. -/
def IsAbelianGroup (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := IsAssociative Q ∧ IsCommutative Q

/-- A loop has *exponent `n`* if `x ^ n = 1` for every `x` (the exponent is not required to be
minimal). -/
def HasExponent (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ x : Q, x ^ n = 1

/-- A loop is *torsion free* if no element other than `1` has finite order. -/
def IsTorsionFree (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Q) (k : ℕ), 0 < k → x ^ k = 1 → x = 1

/-- A *Moufang loop* is a loop satisfying the (left) Moufang identity
`x * (y * (x * z)) = ((x * y) * x) * z`. -/
class IsMoufang (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop where
  moufang (x y z : Q) : x * (y * (x * z)) = x * y * x * z

/-- A *left Bol loop* is a loop satisfying the left Bol identity
`x * (y * (x * z)) = (x * (y * x)) * z`. -/
class IsLeftBol (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop where
  left_bol (x y z : Q) : x * (y * (x * z)) = x * (y * x) * z

/-- A loop is *flexible* if `(x * y) * x = x * (y * x)` for all `x`, `y`. -/
def IsFlexible (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y : Q, x * y * x = x * (y * x)

/-- A loop has the *antiautomorphic inverse property* if `(x * y)^λ = y^λ * x^λ` for all
`x`, `y`, where `x^λ` is the left inverse (this forces inverses to be two-sided). -/
def HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : Q, leftInv (x * y) = leftInv y * leftInv x

/-- A loop is *Osborn* if it satisfies `x * ((y * z) * x) = (x^λ ⧵ y) * (z * x)`, where `x^λ` is
the left inverse of `x`. -/
def IsOsborn (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y z : Q, x * (y * z * x) = (leftInv x ⧵ y) * (z * x)

/-- Two loops `Q` and `Q'` are *isotopic* if there are bijections `α β γ : Q → Q'` with
`γ (x * y) = α x * β y` for all `x`, `y`; `Q'` is then called a (loop) isotope of `Q`. -/
def IsIsotope (Q : Type u) (Q' : Type v) [Loop Q] [Loop Q'] : Prop :=
  ∃ α β γ : Q ≃ Q', ∀ x y : Q, γ (x * y) = α x * β y

/-- A loop is *universally flexible* if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible. -/
def IsUniversallyFlexible (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q' : Type u) [Loop Q'], IsIsotope Q Q' → IsFlexible Q'

/-- A loop is *middle Bol* if every one of its loop isotopes has the antiautomorphic inverse
property. -/
def IsMiddleBol (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q' : Type u) [Loop Q'], IsIsotope Q Q' → HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty Q'

end Loop

open Loop

/-- A *subloop* of a loop `Q` is a subset containing `1` and closed under multiplication and both
divisions. -/
structure Subloop (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] where
  /-- The underlying set of the subloop. -/
  carrier : Set Q
  one_mem' : (1 : Q) ∈ carrier
  mul_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a * b ∈ carrier
  ldiv_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a ⧵ b ∈ carrier
  div_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a / b ∈ carrier

namespace Subloop

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

instance : SetLike (Subloop Q) Q where
  coe := carrier
  coe_injective' := by
    rintro ⟨_, _, _, _, _⟩ ⟨_, _, _, _, _⟩ h
    congr

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma one_mem (S : Subloop Q) : (1 : Q) ∈ S := S.one_mem'

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_mem (S : Subloop Q) {a b : Q} (ha : a ∈ S) (hb : b ∈ S) : a * b ∈ S :=
  S.mul_mem' ha hb

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma ldiv_mem (S : Subloop Q) {a b : Q} (ha : a ∈ S) (hb : b ∈ S) : a ⧵ b ∈ S :=
  S.ldiv_mem' ha hb

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma div_mem (S : Subloop Q) {a b : Q} (ha : a ∈ S) (hb : b ∈ S) : a / b ∈ S :=
  S.div_mem' ha hb

/-- A subloop is itself a loop. -/
instance (S : Subloop Q) : Loop S where
  mul a b := ⟨a * b, S.mul_mem a.2 b.2⟩
  one := ⟨1, S.one_mem⟩
  one_mul a := Subtype.ext (one_mul (a : Q))
  mul_one a := Subtype.ext (mul_one (a : Q))
  mul_left_bijective a :=
    ⟨fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext (mul_left_cancel (congrArg Subtype.val h)),
      fun b => ⟨⟨a ⧵ b, S.ldiv_mem a.2 b.2⟩, Subtype.ext (mul_ldiv (a : Q) b)⟩⟩
  mul_right_bijective a :=
    ⟨fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext (mul_right_cancel (congrArg Subtype.val h)),
      fun b => ⟨⟨b / a, S.div_mem b.2 a.2⟩, Subtype.ext (rdiv_mul (b : Q) a)⟩⟩

/-- The whole loop, as a subloop of itself. -/
instance : Top (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨{ carrier := Set.univ
     one_mem' := trivial
     mul_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial
     ldiv_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial
     div_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial }⟩

/-- The trivial subloop `{1}`. -/
instance : Bot (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨{ carrier := {1}
     one_mem' := rfl
     mul_mem' := fun ha hb => by simp_all
     ldiv_mem' := fun ha hb => by
       simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at *
       subst ha hb
       simpa using ldiv_mul (1 : Q) 1
     div_mem' := fun ha hb => by
       simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at *
       subst ha hb
       simpa using mul_rdiv (1 : Q) 1 }⟩

instance : OrderTop (Subloop Q) where
  le_top _ _ _ := trivial

@[ext, category API, AMS 20]
lemma ext {S T : Subloop Q} (h : ∀ x, x ∈ S ↔ x ∈ T) : S = T := SetLike.ext h

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma mem_top (x : Q) : x ∈ (⊤ : Subloop Q) := trivial

@[simp, category API, AMS 20]
lemma mem_bot {x : Q} : x ∈ (⊥ : Subloop Q) ↔ x = 1 := Iff.rfl

/-- A subloop `N` of `Q` is *normal* if `x N = N x`, `(x N) y = x (N y)` and `x (y N) = (x y) N`
for all `x y : Q` (Bruck). -/
def IsNormal (N : Subloop Q) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : Q,
    (fun n => x * n) '' N = (fun n => n * x) '' N ∧
    (fun n => x * n * y) '' N = (fun n => x * (n * y)) '' N ∧
    (fun n => x * (y * n)) '' N = (fun n => x * y * n) '' N

end Subloop

namespace Loop

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

/-- A set `s` *generates* the loop `Q` if no proper subloop contains it. -/
def IsGeneratedBy (s : Set Q) : Prop := ∀ S : Subloop Q, s ⊆ S → S = ⊤

/-- A loop is *finitely generated* if it is generated by a finite set. -/
def IsFinitelyGenerated (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∃ s : Finset Q, IsGeneratedBy (s : Set Q)

/-- A loop is *simple* if it is nontrivial and its only normal subloops are `⊥` and `⊤`. -/
def IsSimple (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  Nontrivial Q ∧ ∀ N : Subloop Q, N.IsNormal → N = ⊥ ∨ N = ⊤

/-- The *Frattini subloop* `Φ(Q)`: the intersection of all maximal subloops of `Q` (the whole
loop `Q` if there are none). -/
def frattini (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Subloop Q where
  carrier := {x | ∀ S : Subloop Q, IsCoatom S → x ∈ S}
  one_mem' _ _ := Subloop.one_mem _
  mul_mem' ha hb S hS := S.mul_mem (ha S hS) (hb S hS)
  ldiv_mem' ha hb S hS := S.ldiv_mem (ha S hS) (hb S hS)
  div_mem' ha hb S hS := S.div_mem (ha S hS) (hb S hS)

/-- The *center* `Z(Q)` of a loop: the elements that commute and associate with all elements. -/
def center (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Set Q :=
  {a | ∀ x y : Q, a * x = x * a ∧ a * x * y = a * (x * y) ∧ x * a * y = x * (a * y) ∧
    x * y * a = x * (y * a)}

/-- A multiplicative map `φ : Q → Q'` from a loop `Q` (a loop homomorphism, when `Q'` is a loop)
*realises `Q'` as the quotient loop `Q / N`* if it is surjective with kernel `N`. -/
def IsQuotientHom {Q' : Type v} [MulOneClass Q'] (N : Set Q) (φ : Q →ₙ* Q') : Prop :=
  Function.Surjective φ ∧ ∀ x, φ x = 1 ↔ x ∈ N

/-- `IsNilpotentOfClassLE n Q` says that the loop `Q` is centrally nilpotent of class at most `n`:
`Q` is trivial when `n = 0`, and for `n + 1` the quotient `Q / Z(Q)` (realised as any
surjective homomorphic image with kernel `Z(Q)`) is nilpotent of class at most `n`. -/
def IsNilpotentOfClassLE : ℕ → (Q : Type u) → [Loop Q] → Prop
  | 0, Q, _ => Subsingleton Q
  | n + 1, Q, _ => ∃ (Q' : Type u) (_ : Loop Q') (φ : Q →ₙ* Q'),
      IsQuotientHom (center Q) φ ∧ IsNilpotentOfClassLE n Q'

/-- A loop is (centrally) *nilpotent* if it is nilpotent of some finite class. -/
def IsNilpotent (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∃ n, IsNilpotentOfClassLE n Q

/-- `IsSolvableOfLengthLE n Q` says that the loop `Q` has a subnormal series of length at most `n`
with abelian group factors: `Q` is trivial when `n = 0`, and for `n + 1` there is a normal
subloop `N` such that `Q / N` is an abelian group and `N` is solvable of length at most `n`. -/
def IsSolvableOfLengthLE : ℕ → (Q : Type u) → [Loop Q] → Prop
  | 0, Q, _ => Subsingleton Q
  | n + 1, Q, _ => ∃ (N : Subloop Q) (Q' : Type u) (_ : Loop Q') (φ : Q →ₙ* Q'),
      IsQuotientHom (N : Set Q) φ ∧ IsAbelianGroup Q' ∧ IsSolvableOfLengthLE n N

/-- A loop is *solvable* if it has a finite subnormal series with abelian group factors. -/
def IsSolvable (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∃ n, IsSolvableOfLengthLE n Q

/-- The *multiplication group* `Mlt(Q)`: the permutation group generated by all left and right
translations. -/
def multiplicationGroup (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Q) :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range leftMul ∪ Set.range rightMul)

/-- The *inner mapping group* `Inn(Q)`: the stabiliser of `1` in the multiplication group. -/
def innerMappingGroup (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Q) :=
  multiplicationGroup Q ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm Q) (1 : Q)

/-- An *automorphic loop* is a loop all of whose inner mappings are automorphisms. -/
def IsAutomorphic (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ θ ∈ innerMappingGroup Q, ∀ x y : Q, θ (x * y) = θ x * θ y

/-- The *conjugacy classes* of a loop are the orbits of its inner mapping group. They are
*nontrivial* if they are not just `{1}` and `Q \ {1}`, i.e. some two nonidentity elements lie in
different orbits of `Inn(Q)`. -/
def HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : Q, x ≠ 1 ∧ y ≠ 1 ∧ ∀ θ ∈ innerMappingGroup Q, θ x ≠ y

/-- The *distance* between two loop structures on the same set: the number of pairs `(a, b)` at
which the two multiplication tables differ. -/
def tableDist (L₁ L₂ : Loop Q) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {p : Q × Q // L₁.mul p.1 p.2 ≠ L₂.mul p.1 p.2}

/-- A class `P` of loops is *quadratic* if there is `α > 0` such that any two loops from the
class on the same finite set of order `n` at distance `< α n²` are isomorphic. -/
def IsQuadraticClass (P : ∀ Q : Type, Loop Q → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∀ (Q : Type) [Finite Q] (L₁ L₂ : Loop Q), P Q L₁ → P Q L₂ →
    (tableDist L₁ L₂ : ℝ) < α * (Nat.card Q : ℝ) ^ 2 →
      Nonempty (@MulEquiv Q Q L₁.toMul L₂.toMul)

end Loop

/-- Terms in the language of loops (`1`, `*`, left division `⧵`, right division `/`) with
variables from `α`. -/
inductive Term (α : Type) : Type
  | var : α → Term α
  | one : Term α
  | mul : Term α → Term α → Term α
  | ldiv : Term α → Term α → Term α
  | div : Term α → Term α → Term α

namespace Term

variable {α : Type} {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

/-- Evaluate a term in a loop `Q` under an assignment `f` of the variables. -/
def eval (f : α → Q) : Term α → Q
  | var a => f a
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => eval f s * eval f t
  | ldiv s t => eval f s ⧵ eval f t
  | div s t => eval f s / eval f t

/-- Two terms are *Moufang equivalent* if they take the same value under every assignment in
every Moufang loop, i.e. `s = t` is an identity of the variety of Moufang loops. -/
instance moufangSetoid (α : Type) : Setoid (Term α) where
  r s t := ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M] [IsMoufang M] (f : α → M), s.eval f = t.eval f
  iseqv :=
    { refl := fun _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
      symm := fun h M _ _ f => (h M f).symm
      trans := fun h₁ h₂ M _ _ f => (h₁ M f).trans (h₂ M f) }

end Term

/-- The *free Moufang loop* `MF(α)` on the set `α` of free generators: the loop of all terms
modulo the identities of Moufang loops. -/
def FreeMoufangLoop (α : Type) : Type := Quotient (Term.moufangSetoid α)

namespace FreeMoufangLoop

variable {α : Type}

instance : Loop (FreeMoufangLoop α) where
  one := ⟦.one⟧
  mul := Quotient.map₂ .mul fun _ _ h₁ _ _ h₂ M _ _ f => by
    simp only [Term.eval, h₁ M f, h₂ M f]
  one_mul a := Quotient.inductionOn a fun t => Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => by
    simp [Term.eval]
  mul_one a := Quotient.inductionOn a fun t => Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => by
    simp [Term.eval]
  mul_left_bijective a := Quotient.inductionOn a fun s => ⟨fun x y => by
      refine Quotient.inductionOn₂ x y fun t₁ t₂ h => Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => ?_
      exact mul_left_cancel (Quotient.exact h M f),
    fun x => Quotient.inductionOn x fun t => ⟨⟦.ldiv s t⟧, Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => by
      simp [Term.eval]⟩⟩
  mul_right_bijective a := Quotient.inductionOn a fun s => ⟨fun x y => by
      refine Quotient.inductionOn₂ x y fun t₁ t₂ h => Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => ?_
      exact mul_right_cancel (Quotient.exact h M f),
    fun x => Quotient.inductionOn x fun t => ⟨⟦.div t s⟧, Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => by
      simp [Term.eval]⟩⟩

instance : IsMoufang (FreeMoufangLoop α) where
  moufang x y z := Quotient.inductionOn₃ x y z fun _ _ _ => Quotient.sound fun M _ _ f => by
    simp only [Term.eval]
    exact IsMoufang.moufang _ _ _

/-- The free generators of the free Moufang loop. -/
def of (a : α) : FreeMoufangLoop α := ⟦.var a⟧

end FreeMoufangLoop

namespace Loop

/-- The identity `s = t` (in the language of loops, with variables indexed by `ℕ`) is a *law* of
the loop `Q` if it holds under every assignment of the variables in `Q`. -/
def IsLaw (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] (s t : Term ℕ) : Prop := ∀ f : ℕ → Q, s.eval f = t.eval f

/-- The laws of `Q` have a *finite basis* if there is a finite set `B` of laws of `Q` such that
every law of `Q` holds in every loop satisfying all identities in `B` (i.e. is a consequence
of `B`). -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Finset (Term ℕ × Term ℕ), (∀ p ∈ B, IsLaw Q p.1 p.2) ∧
    ∀ s t : Term ℕ, IsLaw Q s t →
      ∀ (R : Type) [Loop R], (∀ p ∈ B, IsLaw R p.1 p.2) → IsLaw R s t

/-- A Moufang loop is flexible: `(x * y) * x = x * (y * x)`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsMoufang.isFlexible (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] [IsMoufang Q] : IsFlexible Q := fun x y => by
  simpa using (IsMoufang.moufang x y (1 : Q)).symm

/-- Every Moufang loop is a left Bol loop. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsMoufang.isLeftBol (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] [IsMoufang Q] : IsLeftBol Q where
  left_bol x y z := by rw [IsMoufang.moufang, IsMoufang.isFlexible Q x y]

/-- A loop is nilpotent of class at most `0` if and only if it is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma isNilpotentOfClassLE_zero_iff (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] :
    IsNilpotentOfClassLE 0 Q ↔ Subsingleton Q := Iff.rfl

end Loop

/-- A (not necessarily associative) ring is *alternative* if it satisfies the left and right
alternative laws `(a * a) * b = a * (a * b)` and `(b * a) * a = b * (a * a)`. -/
def IsAlternative (A : Type u) [Mul A] : Prop :=
  (∀ a b : A, a * a * b = a * (a * b)) ∧ ∀ a b : A, b * a * a = b * (a * a)

/- ## Open problems (Moufang loops) -/

/--
**Abelian by cyclic groups resulting in Moufang loops, (i).**
Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal abelian subgroup (associative subloop) $M$ of odd order
such that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger than $3$. Is $L$ a group?

The quotient $L/M$ is realised as any surjective homomorphic image of $L$ with kernel $M$.
The hypothesis that $L/M$ has order bigger than $3$ is important: there is a commutative Moufang
loop of order $81$ with a normal commutative subgroup of order $27$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L] (M : Subloop L), M.IsNormal →
      IsAbelianGroup M → Odd (Nat.card M) →
      ∀ (C : Type*) [Group C] [IsCyclic C] (φ : L →ₙ* C), IsQuotientHom (M : Set L) φ →
      3 < Nat.card C → IsAssociative L := by
  sorry

/--
**Abelian by cyclic groups resulting in Moufang loops, (ii).**
Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal abelian subgroup (associative subloop) $M$ of odd order
such that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger than $3$. If the orders of $M$ and $L/M$ are
relatively prime, is $L$ a group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i.variants.coprime :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L] (M : Subloop L), M.IsNormal →
      IsAbelianGroup M → Odd (Nat.card M) →
      ∀ (C : Type*) [Group C] [IsCyclic C] (φ : L →ₙ* C), IsQuotientHom (M : Set L) φ →
      3 < Nat.card C → Nat.Coprime (Nat.card M) (Nat.card C) → IsAssociative L := by
  sorry

/--
**Embedding CMLs of period 3 into alternative algebras.**
Conjecture: any finite commutative Moufang loop of period $3$ (i.e. $x^3 = 1$ for all $x$) can be
embedded into a commutative alternative algebra.

Here an embedding is an injective multiplicative map $L \to A$ sending $1$ to $1$, i.e. an
isomorphism of $L$ onto a subloop of the multiplicative loop of invertible elements of a unital
commutative alternative algebra $A$ over some field $F$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ii :
    ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L] [Finite L], Loop.IsCommutative L → HasExponent L 3 →
      ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (A : Type) (_ : NonAssocCommRing A) (_ : Module F A)
        (_ : IsScalarTower F A A) (_ : SMulCommClass F A A),
        IsAlternative A ∧ ∃ φ : L →ₙ* A, Function.Injective φ ∧ φ 1 = 1 := by
  sorry

/--
**Frattini subloop for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture: let $L$ be a finite Moufang loop and $\Phi(L)$ the intersection of all maximal
subloops of $L$. Then $\Phi(L)$ is a normal nilpotent subloop of $L$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iii :
    ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L] [Finite L],
      (Loop.frattini L).IsNormal ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent (Loop.frattini L) := by
  sorry

/--
**The restricted Burnside problem for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture: let $M$ be a finite Moufang loop of exponent $n$ with $m$ generators. Then there
exists a function $f(n, m)$ such that $|M| < f(n, m)$.

The exponent $n$ is a positive integer, and "$m$ generators" means that $M$ is generated by the
values of some map $\mathrm{Fin}\ m \to M$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iv :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ), 0 < n →
      ∀ (M : Type*) [Loop M] [IsMoufang M] [Finite M], HasExponent M n →
        (∃ g : Fin m → M, IsGeneratedBy (Set.range g)) → Nat.card M < f n m := by
  sorry

/--
**The Sanov and M. Hall theorems for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture: let $L$ be a finitely generated Moufang loop of exponent $4$ or $6$. Then $L$ is
finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.v :
    ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L], IsFinitelyGenerated L →
      (HasExponent L 4 ∨ HasExponent L 6) → Finite L := by
  sorry

/--
**Torsion in free Moufang loops.**
Let $MF_n$ be the free Moufang loop with $n$ generators.
Conjecture: $MF_3$ is torsion free but $MF_n$ with $n > 4$ is not.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vi :
    IsTorsionFree (FreeMoufangLoop (Fin 3)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, 4 < n → ¬ IsTorsionFree (FreeMoufangLoop (Fin n)) := by
  sorry

/- ## Open problems (Bol loops) -/

/--
**Are two Bol loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
Let $(Q, *)$, $(Q, +)$ be two quasigroups defined on the same underlying set $Q$. The distance
$d(*, +)$ is the number of pairs $(a, b)$ in $Q \times Q$ such that $a * b \neq a + b$. Call a
class of finite quasigroups quadratic if there is a positive real number $\alpha$ such that any
two quasigroups $(Q, *)$, $(Q, +)$ of order $n$ from the class satisfying $d(*, +) < \alpha n^2$
are isomorphic. Are Moufang loops quadratic?

Drápal proved that groups are quadratic with $\alpha = 1/9$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q L => @IsMoufang Q L := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Bol loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
Are (left) Bol loops quadratic, in the sense of
`problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii.variants.bol :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q L => @IsLeftBol Q L := by
  sorry

/--
**Universally flexible loop that is not middle Bol.**
A loop is universally flexible if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible, that is, satisfies
$(xy)x = x(yx)$. A loop is middle Bol if every one of its loop isotopes has the antiautomorphic
inverse property, that is, satisfies $(xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1}$. Is there a finite, universally
flexible loop that is not middle Bol?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.viii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsUniversallyFlexible Q ∧
      ¬ IsMiddleBol Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes.**
Is there a finite simple nonassociative (left) Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes?

The conjugacy classes of a loop are the orbits of its inner mapping group; they are nontrivial
if they are not just $\{1\}$ and $Q \setminus \{1\}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ix :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsLeftBol Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧
      ¬ IsAssociative Q ∧ HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses Q := by
  sorry

/- ## Open problems (nilpotency and solvability) -/

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group is nilpotent. Is $Q$ nilpotent?

The answer is affirmative if $Q$ is finite (Niemenmaa 2009); the general case is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      Group.IsNilpotent (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture, solvable version.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group is nilpotent. Is $Q$ solvable?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x.variants.solvable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      Group.IsNilpotent (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsSolvable Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. Is $Q$ nilpotent?

When the inner mapping group is finite and abelian, $Q$ is nilpotent (Niemenmaa–Kepka), so the
question is open only in the infinite case.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      IsMulCommutative (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group, bounded class.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. If $Q$ is nilpotent, is there a bound on the
nilpotency class of $Q$? That is, is there $c$ such that every nilpotent loop with abelian inner
mapping group has nilpotency class at most $c$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.bounded_class :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      IsMulCommutative (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q →
        IsNilpotentOfClassLE c Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group, class higher than 3.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. Can the nilpotency class of $Q$ be higher
than $3$? That is, is there a nilpotent loop of nilpotency class at least $4$ with abelian inner
mapping group?

Nilpotent loops of class $3$ with abelian inner mapping group (loops of Csörgő type) exist, but
no such loop of class higher than $3$ is known.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.class_gt_three :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), IsMulCommutative (innerMappingGroup Q) ∧
      Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧ ¬ IsNilpotentOfClassLE 3 Q := by
  sorry

/--
**A finite nilpotent loop without a finite basis for its laws.**
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee, Kourovka
Notebook), i.e. does there exist a finite nilpotent loop whose laws are not finitely based?

There is a finite loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee 1979), but it is not
nilpotent.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      ¬ HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Q := by
  sorry

/- ## Open problems (miscellaneous) -/

/--
**Finite simple nonassociative automorphic loop.**
Find a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop, if such a loop exists; i.e. does there
exist a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop?

Such a loop cannot be commutative (Grishkov, Kinyon and Nagy 2013) nor have odd order (Kinyon,
Kunen, Phillips and Vojtěchovský 2013).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧ IsAutomorphic Q ∧
      ¬ IsAssociative Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Universality of Osborn loops.**
A loop is Osborn if it satisfies the identity $x((yz)x) = (x^\lambda \backslash y)(zx)$, where
$x^\lambda$ is the left inverse of $x$. Is every Osborn loop universal, that is, is every isotope
of an Osborn loop Osborn?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiv :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q], IsOsborn Q →
      ∀ (Q' : Type*) [Loop Q'], IsIsotope Q Q' → IsOsborn Q' := by
  sorry

end

end ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table is consistent with the article's open-problem sections. Minor remarks: (1) for slots ix and vii.variants.bol the article just says "Bol loop"; I followed the notes and used left Bol loops (harmless: the properties involved are invariant under passing to the opposite loop, which exchanges left and right Bol). (2) For slot ii the notes describe the embedding as into "elements 1+x"; in a unital algebra every element has that form, so I used the equivalent "injective multiplicative map with φ 1 = 1" (i.e. onto a subloop of the loop of invertible elements).
modeling_decisions: Mathlib has no loops/quasigroups, so the file defines `Loop` (a `MulOneClass` with bijective left and right translations), divisions `⧵` and `/`, left/right inverses, subloops, `⊤`/`⊥`, and the standard loop-theoretic notions. All of this is bespoke and should be reviewed.

Powers `x ^ n` are defined recursively as `x ^ (n+1) = x * x ^ n`. All slots using powers (ii, iv, v, vi) concern Moufang loops, which are diassociative, so the bracketing is immaterial there. `HasExponent Q n` is `∀ x, x ^ n = 1` (not necessarily minimal); slot iv adds `0 < n` since exponent 0 is vacuous.
Moufang loops are defined by the left Moufang identity `x(y(xz)) = ((xy)x)z`; left Bol loops by `x(y(xz)) = (x(yx))z`. An API lemma checks Moufang ⇒ flexible ⇒ left Bol.
Normal subloop (`Subloop.IsNormal`) uses Bruck's coset equations xN = Nx, (xN)y = x(Ny), x(yN) = (xy)N.

Quotient loops are not constructed. `IsQuotientHom N φ` says the multiplicative map φ (onto a loop or group) is surjective with kernel N; by the first isomorphism theorem for loops this realises Q/N up to isomorphism. Slot i uses this: 'L/M is a cyclic group of order > 3' becomes: for any cyclic group C and φ : L →ₙ* C surjective with kernel M, 3 < Nat.card C. The (redundant but literal) hypothesis `M.IsNormal` is kept.

Central nilpotency is defined recursively: class ≤ 0 iff trivial; class ≤ n+1 iff some surjective homomorphic image with kernel exactly Z(Q) has class ≤ n (this mirrors the upper central series Q/Z(Q); the image lives in the same universe as Q). Nilpotency class > 3 is stated as `IsNilpotent ∧ ¬ IsNilpotentOfClassLE 3`, valid since the predicate is monotone in the class bound.

Solvability is defined recursively by subnormal series with abelian-group factors (∃ subloop N which is the kernel of a surjective hom onto a commutative associative loop, with N solvable of smaller length); this is equivalent to Bruck's derived-series definition.

Inner mapping group: `Mlt(Q) = closure(range leftMul ∪ range rightMul) ≤ Perm Q`, `Inn(Q) = Mlt(Q) ⊓ stabilizer 1`. Nilpotent/abelian Inn(Q) uses Mathlib's `Group.IsNilpotent` / `IsMulCommutative` on the subgroup.

Slot ix: 'nontrivial conjugacy classes' is fixed (per the notes) as: two nonidentity elements lie in different Inn(Q)-orbits, i.e. the classes are not just {1} and Q∖{1}. `IsSimple` requires `Nontrivial Q` and that every normal subloop is ⊥ or ⊤.

Slot ii: the algebra is a unital `NonAssocCommRing A` satisfying the left and right alternative laws, equipped with a module structure over an existentially quantified field F with `IsScalarTower F A A` and `SMulCommClass F A A` (Mathlib's convention for non-associative algebras). 'Embedded' = injective `L →ₙ* A` with `φ 1 = 1`. For a nonassociative CML any such algebra must have characteristic 3, so quantifying over all fields is harmless.

Slot iii: `frattini Q` is the subloop `{x | ∀ S, IsCoatom S → x ∈ S}` (intersection of maximal subloops; equals Q when there are none). Nilpotency of Φ(L) uses the induced `Loop` instance on the subtype.

Slot iv: 'm generators' is `∃ g : Fin m → M` whose range generates M, where `IsGeneratedBy s` means no proper subloop contains s. The bound is stated as `∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ n m, 0 < n → ∀ M, ... → Nat.card M < f n m`.

Slot vi: the free Moufang loop `FreeMoufangLoop α` is constructed as loop terms (variables, 1, *, ⧵, /) modulo the relation 's ~ t iff s and t agree under every assignment in every Moufang loop (in `Type`)'; the file proves it is a Moufang loop. This is the standard relatively-free construction; its universal property is not proved. Torsion-free = no x ≠ 1 with x ^ k = 1 for some k > 0.

Slots vii: `IsQuadraticClass P` quantifies over a finite type Q and two loop structures L₁ L₂ on Q (possibly with different identity elements, as in the article), with distance `Nat.card {p : Q × Q // L₁.mul p.1 p.2 ≠ L₂.mul p.1 p.2}` and isomorphism `Nonempty (@MulEquiv Q Q L₁.toMul L₂.toMul)`; α is uniform over all n.

Slots viii, xiv: loop isotopy is `∃ α β γ : Q ≃ Q', ∀ x y, γ (x * y) = α x * β y`; universally flexible / middle Bol / universal Osborn quantify over all loop isotopes (in the same universe for viii; any universe for xiv). The antiautomorphic inverse property is stated with left inverses `(xy)^λ = y^λ x^λ`, which forces two-sided inverses. The Osborn identity is the article's `x((yz)x) = (x^λ ⧵ y)(zx)`.
Slot xii: laws are pairs of loop terms with variables in ℕ; `HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Q` says some finite set B of laws of Q semantically implies (within the class of all loops) every law of Q.
Existential slots use `Type` (universe 0); universal slots use `Type*`.

theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iii :
    ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L] [Finite L],
      (Loop.frattini L).IsNormal ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent (Loop.frattini L) := by
  sorry

/--
**The restricted Burnside problem for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture: let $M$ be a finite Moufang loop of exponent $n$ with $m$ generators. Then there
exists a function $f(n, m)$ such that $|M| < f(n, m)$.

The exponent $n$ is a positive integer, and "$m$ generators" means that $M$ is generated by the
values of some map $\mathrm{Fin}\ m \to M$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iv :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ), 0 < n →
      ∀ (M : Type*) [Loop M] [IsMoufang M] [Finite M], HasExponent M n →
        (∃ g : Fin m → M, IsGeneratedBy (Set.range g)) → Nat.card M < f n m := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes.**
Is there a finite simple nonassociative (left) Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes?

The conjugacy classes of a loop are the orbits of its inner mapping group; they are nontrivial
if they are not just $\{1\}$ and $Q \setminus \{1\}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ix :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsLeftBol Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧
      ¬ IsAssociative Q ∧ HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses Q := by
  sorry

/--
**The Sanov and M. Hall theorems for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture: let $L$ be a finitely generated Moufang loop of exponent $4$ or $6$. Then $L$ is
finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.v :
    ∀ (L : Type*) [Loop L] [IsMoufang L], IsFinitelyGenerated L →
      (HasExponent L 4 ∨ HasExponent L 6) → Finite L := by
  sorry

/--
**Torsion in free Moufang loops.**
Let $MF_n$ be the free Moufang loop with $n$ generators.
Conjecture: $MF_3$ is torsion free but $MF_n$ with $n > 4$ is not.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vi :
    IsTorsionFree (FreeMoufangLoop (Fin 3)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, 4 < n → ¬ IsTorsionFree (FreeMoufangLoop (Fin n)) := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Bol loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
Let $(Q, *)$, $(Q, +)$ be two quasigroups defined on the same underlying set $Q$. The distance
$d(*, +)$ is the number of pairs $(a, b)$ in $Q \times Q$ such that $a * b \neq a + b$. Call a
class of finite quasigroups quadratic if there is a positive real number $\alpha$ such that any
two quasigroups $(Q, *)$, $(Q, +)$ of order $n$ from the class satisfying $d(*, +) < \alpha n^2$
are isomorphic. Are Moufang loops quadratic?

Drápal proved that groups are quadratic with $\alpha = 1/9$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q L => @IsMoufang Q L := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Bol loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
Are (left) Bol loops quadratic, in the sense of
`problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii.variants.bol :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q L => @IsLeftBol Q L := by
  sorry

/--
**Universally flexible loop that is not middle Bol.**
A loop is universally flexible if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible, that is, satisfies
$(xy)x = x(yx)$. A loop is middle Bol if every one of its loop isotopes has the antiautomorphic
inverse property, that is, satisfies $(xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1}$. Is there a finite, universally
flexible loop that is not middle Bol?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.viii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsUniversallyFlexible Q ∧
      ¬ IsMiddleBol Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group is nilpotent. Is $Q$ nilpotent?

The answer is affirmative if $Q$ is finite (Niemenmaa 2009); the general case is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      Group.IsNilpotent (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture, solvable version.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group is nilpotent. Is $Q$ solvable?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x.variants.solvable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      Group.IsNilpotent (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsSolvable Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. Is $Q$ nilpotent?

When the inner mapping group is finite and abelian, $Q$ is nilpotent (Niemenmaa–Kepka), so the
question is open only in the infinite case.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      IsMulCommutative (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group, bounded class.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. If $Q$ is nilpotent, is there a bound on the
nilpotency class of $Q$? That is, is there $c$ such that every nilpotent loop with abelian inner
mapping group has nilpotency class at most $c$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.bounded_class :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q],
      IsMulCommutative (innerMappingGroup Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q →
        IsNilpotentOfClassLE c Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group, class higher than 3.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. Can the nilpotency class of $Q$ be higher
than $3$? That is, is there a nilpotent loop of nilpotency class at least $4$ with abelian inner
mapping group?

Nilpotent loops of class $3$ with abelian inner mapping group (loops of Csörgő type) exist, but
no such loop of class higher than $3$ is known.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.class_gt_three :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), IsMulCommutative (innerMappingGroup Q) ∧
      Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧ ¬ IsNilpotentOfClassLE 3 Q := by
  sorry

/--
**A finite nilpotent loop without a finite basis for its laws.**
Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee, Kourovka
Notebook), i.e. does there exist a finite nilpotent loop whose laws are not finitely based?

There is a finite loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee 1979), but it is not
nilpotent.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      ¬ HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple nonassociative automorphic loop.**
Find a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop, if such a loop exists; i.e. does there
exist a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop?

Such a loop cannot be commutative (Grishkov, Kinyon and Nagy 2013) nor have odd order (Kinyon,
Kunen, Phillips and Vojtěchovský 2013).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧ IsAutomorphic Q ∧
      ¬ IsAssociative Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Universality of Osborn loops.**
A loop is Osborn if it satisfies the identity $x((yz)x) = (x^\lambda \backslash y)(zx)$, where
$x^\lambda$ is the left inverse of $x$. Is every Osborn loop universal, that is, is every isotope
of an Osborn loop Osborn?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiv :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type*) [Loop Q], IsOsborn Q →
      ∀ (Q' : Type*) [Loop Q'], IsIsotope Q Q' → IsOsborn Q' := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory

A *loop* is a set with a binary operation `*` and an identity element `1` such that every
left translation `x ↦ a * x` and every right translation `x ↦ x * a` is a bijection. Loops
generalise groups: a loop is a group if and only if its multiplication is associative.

This file states the open problems on loops from the Wikipedia article
"Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory" which have a precise mathematical statement.
Most of them were posed at the Loops (Prague) and Mile High (Denver) conferences.

Mathlib has no theory of loops, so the basic notions are defined in this file: loops, subloops,
the multiplication group and the inner mapping group, normal subloops, the centre, central
nilpotency, solvability, isotopy, powers and exponents, free Moufang loops, and loop identities.
The main standard references for these notions are the books of Bruck and Pflugfelder.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- R. H. Bruck, *A survey of binary systems*, Springer, 1958.
- H. O. Pflugfelder, *Quasigroups and loops: introduction*, Heldermann, 1990.
-/

namespace ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory

universe u v

open Function

noncomputable section

/-- A *loop* is a set with a multiplication and a two-sided identity element such that
every left translation `x ↦ a * x` and every right translation `x ↦ x * a` is a bijection.
Equivalently, a loop is a quasigroup with an identity element. -/
class Loop (Q : Type u) extends MulOneClass Q where
  /-- Every left translation is a bijection. -/
  mulLeft_bijective (a : Q) : Bijective (a * ·)
  /-- Every right translation is a bijection. -/
  mulRight_bijective (a : Q) : Bijective (· * a)

namespace Loop

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

/-- The left translation `L_a : x ↦ a * x` as a permutation of `Q`. -/
def mulLeftEquiv (a : Q) : Equiv.Perm Q := Equiv.ofBijective _ (mulLeft_bijective a)

/-- The right translation `R_a : x ↦ x * a` as a permutation of `Q`. -/
def mulRightEquiv (a : Q) : Equiv.Perm Q := Equiv.ofBijective _ (mulRight_bijective a)

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma mulLeftEquiv_apply (a x : Q) : mulLeftEquiv a x = a * x := rfl

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma mulRightEquiv_apply (a x : Q) : mulRightEquiv a x = x * a := rfl

/-- Left division `a \ b`: the unique `x` with `a * x = b`. -/
def ldiv (a b : Q) : Q := (mulLeftEquiv a).symm b

/-- Right division `b / a`: the unique `x` with `x * a = b`. -/
def rdiv (b a : Q) : Q := (mulRightEquiv a).symm b

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma mul_ldiv (a b : Q) : a * ldiv a b = b := (mulLeftEquiv a).apply_symm_apply b

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma rdiv_mul (b a : Q) : rdiv b a * a = b := (mulRightEquiv a).apply_symm_apply b

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma ldiv_mul_self (a b : Q) : ldiv a (a * b) = b := (mulLeftEquiv a).symm_apply_apply b

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma rdiv_mul_self (a b : Q) : rdiv (b * a) a = b := (mulRightEquiv a).symm_apply_apply b

/-- The left inverse `x^λ` of `x`, i.e. the unique element with `x^λ * x = 1`. -/
def linv (x : Q) : Q := rdiv 1 x

/-- The right inverse `x^ρ` of `x`, i.e. the unique element with `x * x^ρ = 1`. -/
def rinv (x : Q) : Q := ldiv x 1

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma linv_mul (x : Q) : linv x * x = 1 := rdiv_mul 1 x

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_rinv (x : Q) : x * rinv x = 1 := mul_ldiv x 1

/-- Left-normed powers `x ^ 0 = 1`, `x ^ (n + 1) = x ^ n * x`. In a power-associative loop
(for instance a Moufang or Bol loop) all bracketings of `x * ⋯ * x` agree, so this is *the*
`n`-th power of `x`. -/
def npow (x : Q) : ℕ → Q
  | 0 => 1
  | n + 1 => npow x n * x

instance : Pow Q ℕ := ⟨npow⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma pow_zero' (x : Q) : x ^ 0 = 1 := rfl

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma pow_succ' (x : Q) (n : ℕ) : x ^ (n + 1) = x ^ n * x := rfl

/-- A loop is *associative* if `x * y * z = x * (y * z)` for all `x y z`.
Associative loops are exactly the groups. -/
def IsAssociative (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y z : Q, x * y * z = x * (y * z)

/-- A loop is *Moufang* if it satisfies the Moufang identity
`(x * y) * (z * x) = x * ((y * z) * x)`.
In a loop, this identity is equivalent to each of the other three Moufang identities. -/
def IsMoufang (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y z : Q, (x * y) * (z * x) = x * ((y * z) * x)

/-- A loop is *left Bol* if it satisfies the left Bol identity
`x * (y * (x * z)) = (x * (y * x)) * z`.
Following the source, "Bol loop" means "left Bol loop". -/
def IsLeftBol (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y z : Q, x * (y * (x * z)) = (x * (y * x)) * z

/-- A loop is *flexible* if it satisfies the flexible law `(x * y) * x = x * (y * x)`. -/
def IsFlexible (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∀ x y : Q, (x * y) * x = x * (y * x)

/-- A loop has the *antiautomorphic inverse property* if it has two-sided inverses
(`x^λ = x^ρ`) and satisfies `(x * y)⁻¹ = y⁻¹ * x⁻¹`. -/
def HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  (∀ x : Q, linv x = rinv x) ∧ ∀ x y : Q, linv (x * y) = linv y * linv x

/-- A loop is *Osborn* if it satisfies the identity `x * ((y * z) * x) = (x^λ \ y) * (z * x)`,
where `x^λ` is the left inverse of `x` and `\` is left division. -/
def IsOsborn (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y z : Q, x * ((y * z) * x) = ldiv (linv x) y * (z * x)

/-- A loop `Q'` is a (loop) *isotope* of the loop `Q` if there are bijections `α β γ : Q → Q'`
with `γ (x * y) = α x * β y` for all `x y : Q`. -/
def IsIsotope (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] (Q' : Type v) [Loop Q'] : Prop :=
  ∃ α β γ : Q ≃ Q', ∀ x y : Q, γ (x * y) = α x * β y

/-- A loop `Q` is *universally `P`* (for a property `P` of loops) if every loop isotope of `Q`
satisfies `P`. For instance `IsUniversal IsFlexible Q` says that `Q` is universally flexible,
and `IsUniversal HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty Q` says that `Q` is middle Bol. -/
def IsUniversal (P : (Q : Type u) → [Loop Q] → Prop) (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q' : Type u) [Loop Q'], IsIsotope Q Q' → P Q'

/-- The *centre* of a loop: the elements that commute with all elements and associate with
all pairs of elements (in every position). -/
def center (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Set Q :=
  {a | ∀ x y : Q, a * x = x * a ∧ a * x * y = a * (x * y) ∧ x * a * y = x * (a * y) ∧
    x * y * a = x * (y * a)}

/-- The *multiplication group* `Mlt(Q)` of a loop: the permutation group generated by all
left and right translations. -/
def mlt (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Q) :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range mulLeftEquiv ∪ Set.range mulRightEquiv)

/-- The *inner mapping group* `Inn(Q)` of a loop: the stabiliser of `1` in `Mlt(Q)`. -/
def inn (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Q) :=
  mlt Q ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm Q) (1 : Q)

/-- Two elements of a loop are *conjugate* if they lie in the same orbit of the inner mapping
group. The orbits of `Inn(Q)` are the *conjugacy classes* of the loop `Q` (Johnson–Smith). -/
def IsConjugate (x y : Q) : Prop := ∃ φ ∈ inn Q, φ x = y

/-- A loop is *automorphic* if all its inner mappings are automorphisms. -/
def IsAutomorphic (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ φ ∈ inn Q, ∀ x y : Q, φ (x * y) = φ x * φ y

/-- A loop is *torsion-free* if no element other than `1` has finite order. -/
def IsTorsionFree (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Q) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → x ^ n = 1 → x = 1

/-- `gen : ι → F` is a free generating family of the *free Moufang loop* `F` on `ι`: `F` is
Moufang, and every map from `ι` to a Moufang loop extends uniquely to a loop homomorphism. -/
def IsFreeMoufangLoopOn {F : Type u} [Loop F] {ι : Type v} (gen : ι → F) : Prop :=
  IsMoufang F ∧ ∀ (M : Type u) [Loop M], IsMoufang M →
    ∀ g : ι → M, ∃! φ : F →* M, ∀ i, φ (gen i) = g i

/-- The *distance* between two loops `Q₁` and `Q₂` on the same underlying set (the
identification
being given by the bijection `e`): the number of pairs `(a, b)` at which the two multiplication
tables differ. -/
def tableDistance {Q₁ : Type u} {Q₂ : Type v} [Loop Q₁] [Loop Q₂] (e : Q₁ ≃ Q₂) :
    ℕ :=
  {p : Q₁ × Q₁ | e (p.1 * p.2) ≠ e p.1 * e p.2}.ncard

/-- A class `P` of finite loops is *quadratic* (Drápal) if there is a real `α > 0` such that any
two loops of order `n` in the class on the same underlying set whose multiplication tables
differ in fewer than `α n ^ 2` places are isomorphic. -/
def IsQuadraticClass (P : (Q : Type) → [Loop Q] → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∀ (Q₁ Q₂ : Type) [Loop Q₁] [Loop Q₂] [Finite Q₁],
    P Q₁ → P Q₂ → ∀ e : Q₁ ≃ Q₂,
      (tableDistance e : ℝ) < α * (Nat.card Q₁) ^ 2 → Nonempty (Q₁ ≃* Q₂)


@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsAssociative.isMoufang (h : IsAssociative Q) : IsMoufang Q := fun x y z => by
  rw [h x y (z * x), h y z x]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsAssociative.isLeftBol (h : IsAssociative Q) : IsLeftBol Q := fun x y z => by
  rw [h x (y * x) z, h y x z]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isIsotope_self : IsIsotope Q Q :=
  ⟨Equiv.refl Q, Equiv.refl Q, Equiv.refl Q, fun _ _ => rfl⟩

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem tableDistance_refl : tableDistance (Equiv.refl Q) = 0 := by
  simp [tableDistance]
end Loop

open Loop

/-- A *subloop* of a loop `Q`: a subset containing `1` and closed under multiplication and
under left and right division. -/
structure Subloop (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] where
  /-- The underlying set. -/
  carrier : Set Q
  one_mem' : (1 : Q) ∈ carrier
  mul_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a * b ∈ carrier
  ldiv_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → ldiv a b ∈ carrier
  rdiv_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → rdiv a b ∈ carrier

namespace Subloop

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

instance : SetLike (Subloop Q) Q where
  coe := carrier
  coe_injective' p q h := by cases p; cases q; congr

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma one_mem (H : Subloop Q) : (1 : Q) ∈ H := H.one_mem'

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma mul_mem (H : Subloop Q) {a b : Q} (ha : a ∈ H) (hb : b ∈ H) : a * b ∈ H :=
  H.mul_mem' ha hb

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma ldiv_mem (H : Subloop Q) {a b : Q} (ha : a ∈ H) (hb : b ∈ H) : ldiv a b ∈ H :=
  H.ldiv_mem' ha hb

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma rdiv_mem (H : Subloop Q) {a b : Q} (ha : a ∈ H) (hb : b ∈ H) : rdiv a b ∈ H :=
  H.rdiv_mem' ha hb

/-- The whole loop, as a subloop. -/
instance : Top (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨{ carrier := Set.univ
     one_mem' := trivial
     mul_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial
     ldiv_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial
     rdiv_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial }⟩

/-- The trivial subloop `{1}`. -/
instance : Bot (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨{ carrier := {1}
     one_mem' := rfl
     mul_mem' := fun ha hb => by
       simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at *
       rw [ha, hb, one_mul]
     ldiv_mem' := fun ha hb => by
       simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at *
       rw [ha, hb]
       simpa using ldiv_mul_self (1 : Q) 1
     rdiv_mem' := fun ha hb => by
       simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at *
       rw [ha, hb]
       simpa using rdiv_mul_self (1 : Q) 1 }⟩

instance : InfSet (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨fun s =>
    { carrier := ⋂ t ∈ s, ↑t
      one_mem' := Set.mem_biInter fun t _ => t.one_mem
      mul_mem' := fun ha hb => Set.mem_biInter fun t ht =>
        t.mul_mem (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 ha t ht) (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 hb t ht)
      ldiv_mem' := fun ha hb => Set.mem_biInter fun t ht =>
        t.ldiv_mem (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 ha t ht) (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 hb t ht)
      rdiv_mem' := fun ha hb => Set.mem_biInter fun t ht =>
        t.rdiv_mem (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 ha t ht) (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 hb t ht) }⟩

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma mem_top (x : Q) : x ∈ (⊤ : Subloop Q) := trivial

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma mem_bot {x : Q} : x ∈ (⊥ : Subloop Q) ↔ x = 1 := Iff.rfl

@[category API, AMS 20, simp]
lemma mem_sInf {S : Set (Subloop Q)} {x : Q} : x ∈ sInf S ↔ ∀ p ∈ S, x ∈ p :=
  Set.mem_iInter₂

@[category API, AMS 20, simp, norm_cast]
lemma coe_sInf (S : Set (Subloop Q)) :
    ((sInf S : Subloop Q) : Set Q) = ⋂ s ∈ S, ↑s := rfl

/-- The subloops of a loop form a complete lattice, ordered by inclusion. -/
instance : CompleteLattice (Subloop Q) :=
  { completeLatticeOfInf (Subloop Q) fun _ =>
      IsGLB.of_image SetLike.coe_subset_coe isGLB_biInf with
    bot := ⊥
    bot_le := fun H x hx => by
      rw [mem_bot] at hx
      rw [hx]
      exact H.one_mem
    top := ⊤
    le_top := fun _ x _ => mem_top x }

/-- The subloop generated by a set. -/
def closure (S : Set Q) : Subloop Q := sInf {H | S ⊆ H}

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma subset_closure {S : Set Q} : S ⊆ closure S := fun _ hx => mem_sInf.2 fun _ hH => hH hx

/-- A subloop is itself a loop. -/
instance (H : Subloop Q) : Loop H where
  mul a b := ⟨a * b, H.mul_mem a.2 b.2⟩
  one := ⟨1, H.one_mem⟩
  one_mul a := Subtype.ext (one_mul (a : Q))
  mul_one a := Subtype.ext (mul_one (a : Q))
  mulLeft_bijective a :=
    ⟨fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext ((mulLeft_bijective (a : Q)).1 (congrArg Subtype.val h)),
      fun b => ⟨⟨ldiv a b, H.ldiv_mem a.2 b.2⟩, Subtype.ext (mul_ldiv (a : Q) b)⟩⟩
  mulRight_bijective a :=
    ⟨fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext ((mulRight_bijective (a : Q)).1 (congrArg Subtype.val h)),
      fun b => ⟨⟨rdiv b a, H.rdiv_mem b.2 a.2⟩, Subtype.ext (rdiv_mul (b : Q) a)⟩⟩

@[category API, AMS 20, simp, norm_cast]
lemma coe_mul (H : Subloop Q) (a b : H) : ((a * b : H) : Q) = a * b := rfl

@[category API, AMS 20, simp, norm_cast]
lemma coe_one (H : Subloop Q) : ((1 : H) : Q) = 1 := rfl

/-- A subloop `N` of `Q` is *normal* if it is invariant under the inner mapping group `Inn(Q)`.
This is equivalent to Bruck's definition (`x * N = N * x`, `(x * y) * N = x * (y * N)` and
`(N * x) * y = N * (x * y)` for all `x y`), and to `N` being the kernel of a loop
homomorphism. -/
def Normal (N : Subloop Q) : Prop := ∀ φ ∈ inn Q, ∀ x ∈ N, φ x ∈ N

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem normal_top : (⊤ : Subloop Q).Normal := fun _ _ x _ => mem_top x

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem normal_bot : (⊥ : Subloop Q).Normal := fun _ hφ x hx => by
  rw [mem_bot] at hx ⊢
  rw [hx]
  exact hφ.2

end Subloop

namespace Loop

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

/-- A loop is *simple* if it is nontrivial and its only normal subloops are `{1}` and itself. -/
def IsSimple (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  Nontrivial Q ∧ ∀ N : Subloop Q, N.Normal → N = ⊥ ∨ N = ⊤

/-- The *Frattini subloop* `Φ(Q)`: the intersection of all maximal subloops of `Q`
(which is `Q` itself if there are no maximal subloops). -/
def frattini (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Subloop Q := Order.radical (Subloop Q)

/-- `IsNilpotentOfClassLE n Q` means that the loop `Q` is centrally nilpotent of class at most
`n`: `Q` is trivial when `n = 0`, and for `n + 1` there is a surjective loop homomorphism
`f : Q → Q'` whose kernel is contained in the centre of `Q` and whose target `Q'` (a copy of
`Q / ker f`) is nilpotent of class at most `n`. Equivalently, `Q` has a central series of
length at most `n`. -/
def IsNilpotentOfClassLE : ℕ → (Q : Type u) → [Loop Q] → Prop
  | 0, Q, _ => Subsingleton Q
  | n + 1, Q, _ => ∃ (Q' : Type u) (_ : Loop Q') (f : Q →* Q'),
      Surjective f ∧ (∀ x, f x = 1 → x ∈ center Q) ∧ IsNilpotentOfClassLE n Q'

/-- A loop is *(centrally) nilpotent* if it is nilpotent of some finite class. -/
def IsNilpotent (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∃ n, IsNilpotentOfClassLE n Q

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isNilpotentOfClassLE_zero_iff : IsNilpotentOfClassLE 0 Q ↔ Subsingleton Q := Iff.rfl

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem mem_center_of_isNilpotentOfClassLE_one (h : IsNilpotentOfClassLE 1 Q) (x : Q) :
    x ∈ center Q := by
  obtain ⟨Q', _, f, -, hf, hQ'⟩ := h
  exact hf x (@Subsingleton.elim _ hQ' _ _)

/-- `IsSolvableOfLengthLE n Q` means that the loop `Q` has a subnormal series
`1 = Q₀ ⊴ Q₁ ⊴ ⋯ ⊴ Qₙ = Q` of length at most `n` in which each `Qᵢ₊₁ / Qᵢ` is an abelian
group: `Q` is trivial when `n = 0`, and for `n + 1` there is a loop homomorphism `f` from
`Q` to an abelian group whose kernel `N` is solvable of length at most `n`. -/
def IsSolvableOfLengthLE : ℕ → (Q : Type u) → [Loop Q] → Prop
  | 0, Q, _ => Subsingleton Q
  | n + 1, Q, _ => ∃ (N : Subloop Q) (A : Type u) (_ : CommGroup A) (f : Q →* A),
      (∀ x, f x = 1 ↔ x ∈ N) ∧ IsSolvableOfLengthLE n N

/-- A loop is *solvable* if it has a subnormal series of finite length with abelian group
factors. -/
def IsSolvable (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop := ∃ n, IsSolvableOfLengthLE n Q

/-- A (not necessarily associative or unital) ring or algebra is *alternative* if it satisfies
the left and right alternative laws `(x * x) * y = x * (x * y)` and `(y * x) * x = y * (x * x)`. -/
def IsAlternative (A : Type u) [Mul A] : Prop :=
  (∀ x y : A, x * x * y = x * (x * y)) ∧ ∀ x y : A, y * x * x = y * (x * x)

end Loop

/-- Terms in the language of loops, with binary operations `*`, `\` (left division) and
`/` (right division), the constant `1`, and variables indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LoopTerm : Type
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  | one : LoopTerm
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm

namespace LoopTerm

variable {Q : Type u} [Loop Q]

/-- Evaluation of a loop term in a loop `Q` under an assignment `σ` of the variables. -/
def eval (σ : ℕ → Q) : LoopTerm → Q
  | var n => σ n
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => eval σ s * eval σ t
  | ldiv s t => Loop.ldiv (eval σ s) (eval σ t)
  | rdiv s t => Loop.rdiv (eval σ s) (eval σ t)

end LoopTerm

namespace Loop

/-- A loop `Q` *satisfies* the law (identity) `s = t` if `s` and `t` evaluate to the same
element of `Q` under every assignment of the variables. -/
def Satisfies (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] (e : LoopTerm × LoopTerm) : Prop :=
  ∀ σ : ℕ → Q, e.1.eval σ = e.2.eval σ

/-- The *laws* of a loop `Q`: the set of all identities satisfied by `Q`. -/
def laws (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Set (LoopTerm × LoopTerm) := {e | Satisfies Q e}

/-- The laws of a loop `Q` have a *finite basis* if there is a finite set `B` of laws of `Q`
such that every loop satisfying all laws in `B` satisfies all laws of `Q`. -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (Q : Type u) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Set (LoopTerm × LoopTerm), B.Finite ∧ B ⊆ laws Q ∧
    ∀ (Q' : Type u) [Loop Q'], (∀ e ∈ B, Satisfies Q' e) → laws Q ⊆ laws Q'

end Loop

/-- Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal abelian subgroup (i.e. associative subloop) $M$ of
odd order such that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger than $3$. Is $L$ a group?

Proposed by Michael Kinyon, based on Chein and Rajah (2000). The condition "$M$ is a normal
subloop of $L$ with $L/M ≅ C$" is expressed by saying that $M$ is the kernel of a surjective
loop homomorphism $f : L → C$. The bound $3$ is sharp: there is a commutative Moufang loop of
order $81$ with a normal abelian subgroup of order $27$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L →
      ∀ (C : Type) [Group C] [IsCyclic C], 3 < Nat.card C →
      ∀ (f : L →* C), Surjective f →
      ∀ (M : Set L), (∀ x, x ∈ M ↔ f x = 1) →
        (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, ∀ c ∈ M, a * b * c = a * (b * c)) →
        (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, a * b = b * a) →
        Odd (Nat.card M) →
        IsAssociative L := by
  sorry

/-- Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal abelian subgroup (i.e. associative subloop) $M$ of
odd order such that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger than $3$. If the orders of $M$ and
$L/M$ are relatively prime, is $L$ a group?

This is the second part of Kinyon's question, a weaker form of
`problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i.variants.coprime :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L →
      ∀ (C : Type) [Group C] [IsCyclic C], 3 < Nat.card C →
      ∀ (f : L →* C), Surjective f →
      ∀ (M : Set L), (∀ x, x ∈ M ↔ f x = 1) →
        (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, ∀ c ∈ M, a * b * c = a * (b * c)) →
        (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, a * b = b * a) →
        Odd (Nat.card M) →
        Nat.Coprime (Nat.card M) (Nat.card C) →
        IsAssociative L := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture** (Grishkov, Loops '03). Any finite commutative Moufang loop of period $3$
(i.e. of exponent $3$: $x^3 = 1$ for all $x$) can be embedded into a commutative alternative
algebra.

Here "embedded" means that there is an injective multiplicative map from the loop into a
commutative alternative (not necessarily associative or unital) algebra over some field.
Grishkov and Shestakov (2011) proved this for the free commutative Moufang loops of exponent
$3$ on fewer than $7$ generators. -/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ii :
    ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L → IsMulCommutative L → Finite L →
      (∀ x : L, x ^ 3 = 1) →
      ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (A : Type) (_ : NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing A) (_ : Module F A)
        (_ : IsScalarTower F A A) (_ : SMulCommClass F A A),
        IsAlternative A ∧
          ∃ φ : L → A, Injective φ ∧ ∀ x y : L, φ (x * y) = φ x * φ y := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture** (Grishkov, Loops '11). Let $L$ be a finite Moufang loop and $Φ(L)$ the
intersection of all maximal subloops of $L$. Then $Φ(L)$ is a normal nilpotent subloop of $L$.

For the trivial loop there are no maximal subloops and $Φ(L) = L$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iii :
    ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L → Finite L →
      (frattini L).Normal ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent (frattini L) := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture** (Grishkov, Loops '11; the restricted Burnside problem for Moufang loops).
Let $M$ be a finite Moufang loop of exponent $n$ with $m$ generators. Then there exists a
function $f(n, m)$ such that $|M| < f(n, m)$.

Here "exponent $n$" means $x^n = 1$ for all $x$ (with $n ≥ 1$, since every loop has
$x^0 = 1$), and "$m$ generators" means that $M$ is generated by some $m$ elements. The case
where $n$ is a prime power is known (Grishkov, Nagy, Grishkov–Sabinina–Zelmanov). -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iv :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ n m : ℕ, 0 < n →
      ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M], IsMoufang M → Finite M → (∀ x : M, x ^ n = 1) →
        (∃ g : Fin m → M, Subloop.closure (Set.range g) = ⊤) →
        Nat.card M < f n m := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture** (Grishkov, Loops '11; the Sanov and M. Hall theorems for Moufang loops).
Let $L$ be a finitely generated Moufang loop of exponent $4$ or $6$. Then $L$ is finite.

Here "exponent $n$" means $x^n = 1$ for all $x$ (not necessarily minimal). -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.v :
    ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L →
      (∃ S : Finset L, Subloop.closure (S : Set L) = ⊤) →
      ((∀ x : L, x ^ 4 = 1) ∨ (∀ x : L, x ^ 6 = 1)) → Finite L := by
  sorry

/-- **Conjecture** (Grishkov, Loops '03). Let $MF_n$ be the free Moufang loop with $n$
generators. Then $MF_3$ is torsion free, but $MF_n$ with $n > 4$ is not.

The free Moufang loop on $n$ generators is characterised (up to isomorphism) by its universal
property `IsFreeMoufangLoopOn`; the conjecture is stated for every loop with this property.
The conjecture says nothing about $n = 4$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vi :
    (∀ (F : Type) [Loop F] (gen : Fin 3 → F), IsFreeMoufangLoopOn gen → IsTorsionFree F) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, 4 < n →
      ∀ (F : Type) [Loop F] (gen : Fin n → F),
        IsFreeMoufangLoopOn gen → ¬ IsTorsionFree F := by
  sorry

/-- Let $(Q, *)$ and $(Q, +)$ be two quasigroups on the same underlying set $Q$. Their distance
$d(*, +)$ is the number of pairs $(a, b) ∈ Q × Q$ with $a * b ≠ a + b$. A class of finite
quasigroups is *quadratic* if there is a real $α > 0$ such that any two quasigroups $(Q, *)$,
$(Q, +)$ of order $n$ from the class with $d(*, +) < α n^2$ are isomorphic.
Are Moufang loops quadratic?

Proposed by Aleš Drápal at Loops '99. Drápal proved that groups are quadratic with
$α = 1/9$ and that $2$-groups are quadratic with $α = 1/4$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass IsMoufang := by
  sorry

/-- Let $(Q, *)$ and $(Q, +)$ be two quasigroups on the same underlying set $Q$. Their distance
$d(*, +)$ is the number of pairs $(a, b) ∈ Q × Q$ with $a * b ≠ a + b$. A class of finite
quasigroups is *quadratic* if there is a real $α > 0$ such that any two quasigroups $(Q, *)$,
$(Q, +)$ of order $n$ from the class with $d(*, +) < α n^2$ are isomorphic.
Are (left) Bol loops quadratic?

Proposed by Aleš Drápal at Loops '99. Since Moufang loops are left Bol loops, a positive
answer implies a positive answer to `problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii.variants.bol :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass IsLeftBol := by
  sorry

/-- A loop is *universally flexible* if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible, that is,
satisfies $(xy)x = x(yx)$. A loop is *middle Bol* if every one of its loop isotopes has the
antiautomorphic inverse property, that is, satisfies $(xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1}$.
Is there a finite, universally flexible loop that is not middle Bol?

Proposed by Michael Kinyon at Loops '03. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.viii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧
      IsUniversal IsFlexible Q ∧ ¬ IsUniversal HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty Q := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a finite simple nonassociative (left) Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes?

Proposed by Kenneth W. Johnson and Jonathan D. H. Smith at the 2nd Mile High Conference (2009).
The conjugacy classes of a loop $Q$ are the orbits of its inner mapping group; they are
*trivial* if the only classes are $\{1\}$ and $Q ∖ \{1\}$ (equivalently, the multiplication
group of $Q$ is doubly transitive). So $Q$ has nontrivial conjugacy classes if two elements
different from $1$ lie in different orbits of $Inn(Q)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ix :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q),
      Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧ ¬ IsAssociative Q ∧ IsLeftBol Q ∧
      ∃ x y : Q, x ≠ 1 ∧ y ≠ 1 ∧ ¬ IsConjugate x y := by
  sorry

/-- **Niemenmaa's conjecture.** Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group $Inn(Q)$ is
nilpotent. Is $Q$ (centrally) nilpotent?

The answer is affirmative if $Q$ is finite (Niemenmaa, 2009); the problem is open in general. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], Group.IsNilpotent (inn Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/-- Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group $Inn(Q)$ is nilpotent. Is $Q$ solvable?

This is a weaker form of `problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x`, since
nilpotent loops are solvable. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x.variants.solvable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], Group.IsNilpotent (inn Q) → Loop.IsSolvable Q := by
  sorry

/-- Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group $Inn(Q)$. Is $Q$ (centrally) nilpotent?

When $Inn(Q)$ is finite and abelian, $Q$ is nilpotent (Niemenmaa and Kepka), so the question is
open only in the infinite case. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsMulCommutative (inn Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/-- Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group. If $Q$ is nilpotent, is there a
(uniform) bound on the nilpotency class of $Q$?

That is, is there a $c$ such that every nilpotent loop with abelian inner mapping group is
nilpotent of class at most $c$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.bounded_class :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsMulCommutative (inn Q) →
      Loop.IsNilpotent Q → IsNilpotentOfClassLE c Q := by
  sorry

/-- Let $Q$ be a nilpotent loop with abelian inner mapping group. Can the nilpotency class of
$Q$ be higher than $3$?

Loops of nilpotency class $3$ with abelian inner mapping group (loops of Csörgő type) exist,
but no such loop of nilpotency class higher than $3$ is known. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.class_gt_three :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), IsMulCommutative (inn Q) ∧
      Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧ ¬ IsNilpotentOfClassLE 3 Q := by
  sorry

/-- Construct a finite nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws
(M. R. Vaughan-Lee, Kourovka Notebook). Formally: does there exist a finite (centrally)
nilpotent loop whose laws have no finite basis?

There is a finite loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee, 1979), but it is not
nilpotent. -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      ¬ HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Q := by
  sorry

/-- Find a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop, if such a loop exists
(Michael Kinyon, Loops '03). Formally: does a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop
exist?

Such a loop cannot be commutative (Grishkov, Kinyon and Nagy, 2013) nor have odd order
(Kinyon, Kunen, Phillips and Vojtěchovský, 2013). -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q),
      Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧ ¬ IsAssociative Q ∧ IsAutomorphic Q := by
  sorry

/-- A loop is *Osborn* if it satisfies the identity $x((yz)x) = (x^λ \backslash y)(zx)$, where
$x^λ$ is the left inverse of $x$. Is every Osborn loop universal, that is, is every (loop)
isotope of an Osborn loop Osborn?

Proposed by Michael Kinyon at the Mile High conference (2005). Moufang and conjugacy closed
loops are Osborn. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiv :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsOsborn Q → IsUniversal IsOsborn Q := by
  sorry

end

end ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory
attempts.decomposition_objections: None of substance. Two minor remarks: (1) In slot i the notes take L/M to be of finite order > 3; the article's text does not literally exclude the infinite cyclic group, but the underlying literature (Chein–Rajah 2000) concerns finite Moufang loops, so the finite reading was followed. (2) In slot iv the exponent must be positive for the statement to be true (x^0 = 1 in every loop); the table does not mention this, and the hypothesis 0 < n was added.
modeling_decisions: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no quasigroup/loop theory at all, so the whole basic theory is built bespoke in the problem file: `Loop` is a `MulOneClass` whose left and right translations are bijective; left/right division, left/right inverses are derived from these bijections.

Normality of a subloop is defined as invariance under the inner mapping group Inn(Q) (the stabiliser of 1 in the multiplication group Mlt(Q) ≤ Equiv.Perm Q). This is the standard equivalent of Bruck's definition and of 'kernel of a loop homomorphism' (confirmed e.g. in arXiv:1111.7138, §1).

Slot i: 'M normal with L/M ≅ C' is encoded without constructing quotient loops, as 'M is the kernel of a surjective loop homomorphism f : L →* C'. Following the decomposition notes, L/M is taken to be a finite cyclic group (`3 < Nat.card C` forces finiteness); M is required to be associative and commutative (an abelian subgroup) with odd `Nat.card`. Finiteness of L follows and is not assumed separately.

Slot ii: 'embedded into a commutative alternative algebra' is read as an injective multiplicative map into a (not necessarily unital or associative) commutative alternative algebra over some field (existentially quantified field). This is equivalent to the Grishkov–Shestakov '1 + x' reading via unitization / Peirce decomposition; the base is taken to be a field since the conjecture says 'algebra'.

Slot iii: Φ(L) is `Order.radical (Subloop L)` (infimum of coatoms of the complete lattice of subloops); for the trivial loop this is ⊤ = L, as the notes prescribe. Nilpotency of Φ(L) is nilpotency of the subloop as a loop in its own right (via a `Loop` instance on subloops).

Central nilpotency is defined recursively: class ≤ 0 iff trivial; class ≤ n+1 iff there is a surjective loop hom f : Q → Q' with ker f ⊆ Z(Q) and Q' of class ≤ n. This is equivalent to the upper-central-series definition (Q/Z(Q) is a quotient of Q/ker f and quotients preserve class ≤ n). Solvability is defined recursively via a hom to an abelian group whose kernel (as a loop) is solvable of smaller length, matching the standard subnormal-series definition.

Powers x^n are left-normed (x^(n+1) = x^n * x); all uses are for Moufang loops, which are diassociative, so bracketing is irrelevant. In slot iv the hypothesis 0 < n is added: x^0 = 1 holds in every loop and would make the conjecture false for n = 0.
Slot iv: 'm generators' is formalised as a family g : Fin m → M whose range generates M (Subloop.closure = ⊤); finitely generated (slot v) as generated by a Finset.

Slot vi: the free Moufang loop MF_n is captured by its universal property (`IsFreeMoufangLoopOn`, quantifying over Moufang loops in the same universe as in Mathlib's `IsFreeGroup.ofUniqueLift`); the conjecture is stated for every loop with this property (unique up to isomorphism). n = 4 is not covered.

Slot vii: two loops 'on the same underlying set' are modelled as two loop types with a bijection e; the distance counts pairs (a,b) with e(a*b) ≠ e a * e b (Set.ncard); the class is restricted to Type 0 (every finite loop lives there up to isomorphism). 'Bol' is taken as left Bol, following the article.

Slot viii/xiv: 'every loop isotope' is quantified over loops Q' in the same universe together with bijections α β γ with γ(xy) = αx·βy. The antiautomorphic inverse property is stated with two-sided inverses (x^λ = x^ρ) plus (xy)^λ = y^λ x^λ; the two-sided condition is in fact implied by the identity.

Slot ix: 'nontrivial conjugacy classes' fixed (as the notes require) to mean that Inn(Q) has at least two distinct orbits on Q∖{1}, i.e. Mlt(Q) is not doubly transitive. 'Simple' includes Nontrivial (as Mathlib's IsSimpleGroup).

Slot xii: laws are identities in the loop signature (·, \, /, 1) with ℕ-indexed variables; 'finite basis' is a finite subset B of the laws of Q such that every loop (in Type) satisfying B satisfies all laws of Q (semantic consequence, equivalent to syntactic derivability by Birkhoff's completeness theorem).

Slot xi.variants.bounded_class: the 'if so' is handled by restricting to nilpotent Q (allowed by the notes); slot xi.variants.class_gt_three asks for a nilpotent loop with abelian Inn(Q) not of class ≤ 3.
Commutativity of loops uses Mathlib's `IsMulCommutative`; associativity ('L is a group') is the bespoke `Loop.IsAssociative` (∀ x y z, x*y*z = x*(y*z)), since an associative loop is a group.
