import FormalConjecturesUtil
/-!
# Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory
*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory)
-/
namespace ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory

structure Loop (α : Type*) where
  mul : α → α → α
  one : α
  ldiv : α → α → α
  rdiv : α → α → α
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  ldiv_spec : ∀ x y, mul x (ldiv x y) = y
  ldiv_unique : ∀ x y z, mul x z = y → z = ldiv x y
  rdiv_spec : ∀ x y, mul (rdiv y x) x = y
  rdiv_unique : ∀ x y z, mul z x = y → z = rdiv y x

namespace Loop
variable {α β : Type*} {n : ℕ}
def inv (L : Loop α) (x : α) := L.ldiv x L.one
structure Hom (L : Loop α) (K : Loop β) where
  toFun : α → β
  map_one : toFun L.one = K.one
  map_mul : ∀ x y, toFun (L.mul x y) = K.mul (toFun x) (toFun y)
def Isomorphic (L : Loop α) (K : Loop β) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : α ≃ β, e L.one = K.one ∧ ∀ x y, e (L.mul x y) = K.mul (e x) (e y)
def Associative (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y z, L.mul (L.mul x y) z = L.mul x (L.mul y z)
def Commutative (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y, L.mul x y = L.mul y x
def Moufang (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y z,
  L.mul (L.mul x y) (L.mul z x) = L.mul x (L.mul (L.mul y z) x)
def LeftBol (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y z,
  L.mul x (L.mul y (L.mul x z)) = L.mul (L.mul x (L.mul y x)) z
def Flexible (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y, L.mul (L.mul x y) x = L.mul x (L.mul y x)
def AntiautomorphicInverse (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y,
  L.inv (L.mul x y) = L.mul (L.inv y) (L.inv x)
def Osborn (L : Loop α) := ∀ x y z,
  L.mul x (L.mul (L.mul y z) x) = L.mul (L.ldiv (L.inv x) y) (L.mul z x)
def pow (L : Loop α) (x : α) : ℕ → α | 0 => L.one | k+1 => L.mul x (L.pow x k)
def HasExponent (L : Loop α) (n : ℕ) := ∀ x, L.pow x n = L.one
def IsTorsion (L : Loop α) (x : α) := ∃ n > 0, L.pow x n = L.one

structure Subloop (L : Loop α) where
  carrier : Set α
  one_mem : L.one ∈ carrier
  mul_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → L.mul x y ∈ carrier
  ldiv_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → L.ldiv x y ∈ carrier
  rdiv_mem : ∀ {x y}, x ∈ carrier → y ∈ carrier → L.rdiv x y ∈ carrier
instance (L : Loop α) : SetLike (Subloop L) α where
  coe := Subloop.carrier
  coe_injective' := by intro A B h; cases A; cases B; cases h; rfl

def leftTranslation (L : Loop α) (a : α) : Equiv.Perm α where
  toFun := L.mul a; invFun := L.ldiv a
  left_inv x := (L.ldiv_unique a (L.mul a x) x rfl).symm
  right_inv := L.ldiv_spec a
def rightTranslation (L : Loop α) (a : α) : Equiv.Perm α where
  toFun := fun x => L.mul x a; invFun := fun x => L.rdiv x a
  left_inv x := (L.rdiv_unique a (L.mul x a) x rfl).symm
  right_inv x := L.rdiv_spec a x
def multiplicationGroup (L : Loop α) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α) :=
  Subgroup.closure {p | ∃ a, p = L.leftTranslation a ∨ p = L.rightTranslation a}
def innerMappingGroup (L : Loop α) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α) :=
  L.multiplicationGroup ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm α) L.one
def IsNormal (L : Loop α) (S : Subloop L) := ∀ p : L.innerMappingGroup, ∀ x ∈ S, p.1 x ∈ S

def CentralModulo (L : Loop α) (A B : Subloop L) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, x ∈ A → x ∈ B) ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ∀ x y,
    L.ldiv (L.mul b x) (L.mul x b) ∈ A ∧
    L.ldiv (L.mul (L.mul b x) y) (L.mul b (L.mul x y)) ∈ A ∧
    L.ldiv (L.mul (L.mul x b) y) (L.mul x (L.mul b y)) ∈ A ∧
    L.ldiv (L.mul (L.mul x y) b) (L.mul x (L.mul y b)) ∈ A
def HasCentralSeries (L : Loop α) (S : Subloop L) (c : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : Fin (c+1) → Subloop L,
    (C 0).carrier = {L.one} ∧ (C ⟨c, Nat.lt_succ_self c⟩).carrier = S.carrier ∧
    (∀ i, L.IsNormal (C i)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin c,
      L.CentralModulo (C ⟨i, Nat.lt_trans i.isLt (Nat.lt_succ_self c)⟩)
        (C ⟨i+1, Nat.succ_lt_succ i.isLt⟩)
def CentrallyNilpotentSubloop (L : Loop α) (S : Subloop L) := ∃ c, L.HasCentralSeries S c
def CentrallyNilpotent (L : Loop α) := ∃ S : Subloop L,
  S.carrier = Set.univ ∧ L.CentrallyNilpotentSubloop S
def NilpotencyClassLE (L : Loop α) (c : ℕ) := ∃ S : Subloop L,
  S.carrier = Set.univ ∧ L.HasCentralSeries S c
def Solvable (L : Loop α) := ∃ (c : ℕ) (C : Fin (c+1) → Subloop L),
  (C 0).carrier = {L.one} ∧ (C ⟨c, Nat.lt_succ_self c⟩).carrier = Set.univ ∧
  (∀ i, L.IsNormal (C i)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin c,
    let A := C ⟨i, Nat.lt_trans i.isLt (Nat.lt_succ_self c)⟩
    let B := C ⟨i+1, Nat.succ_lt_succ i.isLt⟩
    (∀ x, x ∈ A → x ∈ B) ∧ ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B,
      L.ldiv (L.mul x y) (L.mul y x) ∈ A ∧ ∀ z ∈ B,
      L.ldiv (L.mul (L.mul x y) z) (L.mul x (L.mul y z)) ∈ A

def IsMaximal (L : Loop α) (S : Subloop L) := S.carrier ≠ Set.univ ∧ ∀ T : Subloop L,
  (∀ x, x ∈ S → x ∈ T) → T.carrier ≠ S.carrier → T.carrier = Set.univ
def frattini (L : Loop α) : Subloop L where
  carrier := {x | ∀ S : Subloop L, L.IsMaximal S → x ∈ S}
  one_mem := fun S _ => S.one_mem
  mul_mem := fun hx hy S h => S.mul_mem (hx S h) (hy S h)
  ldiv_mem := fun hx hy S h => S.ldiv_mem (hx S h) (hy S h)
  rdiv_mem := fun hx hy S h => S.rdiv_mem (hx S h) (hy S h)
def Generates (L : Loop α) (s : Set α) := ∀ S : Subloop L, s ⊆ S → S.carrier = Set.univ
def GeneratedBy (L : Loop α) (m : ℕ) := ∃ g : Fin m → α, L.Generates (Set.range g)
def Simple (L : Loop α) := ∀ S : Subloop L, L.IsNormal S →
  S.carrier = {L.one} ∨ S.carrier = Set.univ
def Automorphic (L : Loop α) := ∀ p : L.innerMappingGroup, ∀ x y,
  p.1 (L.mul x y) = L.mul (p.1 x) (p.1 y)
def Isotopic (L : Loop α) (K : Loop β) := ∃ f g h : α ≃ β, ∀ x y,
  h (L.mul x y) = K.mul (f x) (g y)
def UniversallyFlexible (L : Loop α) := ∀ K : Loop α, L.Isotopic K → K.Flexible
def MiddleBol (L : Loop α) := ∀ K : Loop α, L.Isotopic K → K.AntiautomorphicInverse
def InnerConjugate (L : Loop α) (x y : α) := ∃ p : L.innerMappingGroup, p.1 x = y
def HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses (L : Loop α) := ∃ x y,
  x ≠ L.one ∧ y ≠ L.one ∧ ¬ L.InnerConjugate x y

def IsCyclicQuotient (L : Loop α) (S : Subloop L) (G : Group β) (f : α → β) : Prop :=
  letI := G
  f L.one = 1 ∧ (∀ x y, f (L.mul x y) = f x * f y) ∧ Function.Surjective f ∧
    (∀ x, f x = 1 ↔ x ∈ S) ∧ IsCyclic β
def IsCommutativeAlternativeRing (A : Type*) (R : NonAssocCommRing A) : Prop :=
  letI := R; ∀ x y : A, x*(x*y)=(x*x)*y ∧ (x*y)*y=x*(y*y)
def EmbedsInCommutativeAlternativeAlgebra (L : Loop α) : Prop :=
  ∃ (A : Type) (R : NonAssocCommRing A), letI := R
    IsCommutativeAlternativeRing A R ∧ (3:A)=0 ∧ ∃ e : α → A,
      Function.Injective e ∧ e L.one=1 ∧ ∀ x y, e (L.mul x y)=e x*e y
def IsFreeMoufang (L : Loop α) (g : Fin n → α) := L.Moufang ∧ ∀ {β : Type} (K : Loop β),
  K.Moufang → ∀ h : Fin n → β, ∃! F : L.Hom K, ∀ i, F.toFun (g i)=h i
noncomputable def tableDistance (L K : Loop α) := Nat.card {p : α×α // L.mul p.1 p.2 ≠ K.mul p.1 p.2}
def Quadratic (P : ∀ {α : Type}, Loop α → Prop) := ∃ a : ℝ, 0<a ∧
  ∀ {α : Type} [Finite α] (L K : Loop α), P L → P K →
    (L.tableDistance K : ℝ) < a*(Nat.card α : ℝ)^2 → L.Isomorphic K

inductive Term | var : ℕ → Term | one | mul : Term → Term → Term
  | ldiv : Term → Term → Term | rdiv : Term → Term → Term
def Term.eval (L : Loop α) (v : ℕ → α) : Term → α
  | .var n => v n | .one => L.one
  | .mul s t => L.mul (s.eval L v) (t.eval L v)
  | .ldiv s t => L.ldiv (s.eval L v) (t.eval L v)
  | .rdiv s t => L.rdiv (s.eval L v) (t.eval L v)
abbrev Law := Term × Term
def Satisfies (L : Loop α) (e : Law) := ∀ v, e.1.eval L v = e.2.eval L v
def laws (L : Loop α) : Set Law := {e | L.Satisfies e}
def HasFiniteBasis (L : Loop α) := ∃ s : Set Law, s.Finite ∧ s ⊆ L.laws ∧
  ∀ {β : Type} (K : Loop β), (∀ e ∈ s, K.Satisfies e) ↔ L.laws ⊆ K.laws
end Loop

namespace problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts
/-- Let `L` be a Moufang loop with a finite normal associative abelian subloop `M` of odd
order. If `L/M` is a finite cyclic group of order greater than three, is `L` a group? -/
@[category research open, AMS 20] theorem i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {α β : Type} (L : Loop α)
    (M : L.Subloop) (G : Group β) [Finite β] (f : α → β), L.Moufang → L.IsNormal M →
    (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ y ∈ M, ∀ z ∈ M, L.mul (L.mul x y) z=L.mul x (L.mul y z)) →
    (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ y ∈ M, L.mul x y=L.mul y x) → Odd (Nat.card M) →
    L.IsCyclicQuotient M G f → 3 < Nat.card β → L.Associative := by sorry
namespace i.variants
/-- Under the hypotheses of part (i), if the orders of `M` and the cyclic quotient `L/M`
are relatively prime, is `L` a group? -/
@[category research open, AMS 20] theorem coprime : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {α β : Type} (L : Loop α)
    (M : L.Subloop) (G : Group β) [Finite β] (f : α → β), L.Moufang → L.IsNormal M →
    (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ y ∈ M, ∀ z ∈ M, L.mul (L.mul x y) z=L.mul x (L.mul y z)) →
    (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ y ∈ M, L.mul x y=L.mul y x) → Odd (Nat.card M) →
    L.IsCyclicQuotient M G f → 3 < Nat.card β → (Nat.card M).Coprime (Nat.card β) →
    L.Associative := by sorry
end i.variants
/-- Every finite commutative Moufang loop of exponent three embeds in a commutative alternative
algebra (here a unital ring of characteristic three). -/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20] theorem ii : ∀ {α : Type} [Finite α] (L : Loop α),
  L.Commutative → L.Moufang → L.HasExponent 3 → L.EmbedsInCommutativeAlternativeAlgebra := by sorry
/-- The Frattini subloop of a finite Moufang loop is normal and centrally nilpotent. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20] theorem iii : ∀ {α : Type} [Finite α] (L : Loop α),
  L.Moufang → L.IsNormal L.frattini ∧ L.CentrallyNilpotentSubloop L.frattini := by sorry
/-- Finite `m`-generated Moufang loops of exponent `n` have uniformly bounded order. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20] theorem iv : ∀ n m, ∃ b, ∀ {α : Type} [Finite α] (L : Loop α),
  L.Moufang → L.HasExponent n → L.GeneratedBy m → Nat.card α < b := by sorry
/-- Every finitely generated Moufang loop of exponent four or six is finite. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20] theorem v : ∀ {α : Type} (L : Loop α), L.Moufang →
  (L.HasExponent 4 ∨ L.HasExponent 6) → (∃ m, L.GeneratedBy m) → Finite α := by sorry
/-- `MF3` is torsion-free, while every `MFn` for `n>4` has nonidentity torsion. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20] theorem vi :
  (∀ {α : Type} (L : Loop α) (g : Fin 3 → α), L.IsFreeMoufang g →

modeling_decisions: A loop is bundled with multiplication, identity, and left/right division operations satisfying the unique-solution axioms. Associativity of this loop is used for “is a group.”
Normal subloops are subloops invariant under the inner mapping group. The multiplication group is generated by left and right translations, and the inner mapping group is its identity stabilizer.

The cyclic quotient hypotheses are represented by a surjective multiplication-preserving map to a finite cyclic group whose kernel is exactly M. This avoids inventing quotient-loop infrastructure while specifying a quotient isomorphic to L/M.

Central nilpotency is modeled by a finite ascending central series of normal subloops. Centrality modulo the preceding term requires commutation and all three associativity positions modulo that term. Nilpotency class at most c means existence of such a series of length c.
Loop solvability is modeled by a finite normal series whose successive factors are associative and commutative, expressed modulo the preceding term.

For part ii, the implicit algebra is fixed to a unital commutative nonassociative ring of characteristic 3 satisfying both alternative laws. Embedding means an injective identity- and multiplication-preserving map; its image consists of invertible elements because the source is a Moufang loop. Elements can equivalently be written as 1+x in the unital ring.
Exponent n means the displayed right-associated power x^n is the identity for every x; it need not be minimal.
An m-generated loop means generated by at most m indexed elements. Thus the restricted Burnside bound has quantifier order ∀ n m, ∃ b, uniformly over all finite loops.
Free Moufang loops are specified by their universal property for maps from Fin n into arbitrary Moufang loops. Torsion means x^k=1 for some positive k.
Quadraticity uses the cardinality of the set of entries where two multiplication tables differ and one positive real constant uniform over all finite carrier types.

Loop isotopy uses three equivalences f, g, h satisfying h(xy)=f(x)·g(y). Universal flexibility, middle Bol, and Osborn universality quantify over loop structures on the same carrier isotopic in this sense, as is conventional for loop isotopes.

Nontrivial conjugacy classes means that two nonidentity elements are in different orbits of the inner mapping group, so the orbit partition is neither {1} plus one class nor merely the identity class.
The Frattini carrier is the intersection of all maximal proper subloops. Its universal formulation makes an empty intersection the whole carrier.

The finite-basis property uses terms in the full loop language (identity, multiplication, left division, right division). A finite subset of the loop's laws is a basis when, semantically over all loops, satisfying it is equivalent to satisfying every law of the original loop.

Parts x and xi quantify over arbitrary loops, including finite loops where the corresponding implication is already known; this states the source's general conjecture without adding an infinitude hypothesis.
The bounded-class variant includes central nilpotency as a hypothesis, implementing the source's “if so.” Class greater than three is expressed as nilpotent but not of class at most 3.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory

Open problems about loops (quasigroups with an identity element), mostly posed at the
Loops (Prague) and Mile High (Denver) conferences. Neither Mathlib nor this repository has a
theory of loops, so this file first sets up the needed notions: loops, subloops, normal
subloops, multiplication and inner mapping groups, central nilpotency, solvability, isotopy,
and the standard loop identities (Moufang, Bol, flexible, Osborn, automorphic).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- R. H. Bruck, *A survey of binary systems*, Springer, 1958.
- H. O. Pflugfelder, *Quasigroups and loops: introduction*, Heldermann, 1990.
-/

namespace ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory

/-
## Loops

A loop is a quasigroup with an identity element. We use the equational definition: a set with
a multiplication, a left division `ldiv a b` (the unique `x` with `a * x = b`), a right division
`b / a` (the unique `x` with `x * a = b`) and a two-sided identity `1`.
-/

/-- A loop: a set with a multiplication `*`, a two-sided identity `1`, a left division `ldiv`
and a right division `/`, such that `a * ldiv a b = b`, `ldiv a (a * b) = b`, `(b / a) * a = b`
and `(a * b) / b = a`. Equivalently, a quasigroup with an identity element. -/
class Loop (Q : Type*) extends MulOneClass Q, Div Q where
  /-- Left division: `ldiv a b` is the unique solution `x` of `a * x = b`. -/
  ldiv : Q → Q → Q
  mul_ldiv_cancel : ∀ a b : Q, a * ldiv a b = b
  ldiv_mul_cancel : ∀ a b : Q, ldiv a (a * b) = b
  /-- Right division: `b / a` is the unique solution `x` of `x * a = b`. -/
  rdiv_mul_cancel : ∀ a b : Q, b / a * a = b
  mul_rdiv_cancel : ∀ a b : Q, a * b / b = a

namespace Loop

variable {Q : Type*} [Loop Q]

/-- Powers in a loop, right-associated: `x ^ 0 = 1` and `x ^ (n + 1) = x ^ n * x`.
In the (diassociative) Moufang loops considered below every bracketing gives the same value. -/
instance : Pow Q ℕ := ⟨fun x n => npowRec n x⟩

/-- The left translation `L_a : x ↦ a * x`, a permutation of `Q`. -/
def leftMul (a : Q) : Equiv.Perm Q :=
  ⟨(a * ·), ldiv a, ldiv_mul_cancel a, mul_ldiv_cancel a⟩

/-- The right translation `R_a : x ↦ x * a`, a permutation of `Q`. -/
def rightMul (a : Q) : Equiv.Perm Q :=
  ⟨(· * a), (· / a), fun b => mul_rdiv_cancel b a, fun b => rdiv_mul_cancel a b⟩

/-- The multiplication group `Mlt(Q)`: the permutation group generated by all left and right
translations. -/
def mlt (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Q) :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range leftMul ∪ Set.range rightMul)

/-- The inner mapping group `Inn(Q)`: the stabilizer of the identity element in `Mlt(Q)`. -/
def inn (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Q) :=
  mlt Q ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm Q) (1 : Q)

/-- A loop is *Moufang* if it satisfies the Moufang identity `(z * x) * (y * z) = (z * (x * y)) * z`
(in a loop this is equivalent to each of the other Moufang identities). -/
def IsMoufang (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y z : Q, z * x * (y * z) = z * (x * y) * z

/-- A loop is *left Bol* if it satisfies `x * (y * (x * z)) = (x * (y * x)) * z`. -/
def IsLeftBol (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y z : Q, x * (y * (x * z)) = x * (y * x) * z

/-- A loop is *flexible* if it satisfies `(x * y) * x = x * (y * x)`. -/
def IsFlexible (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : Q, x * y * x = x * (y * x)

/-- A loop has the *antiautomorphic inverse property* if `(x * y)⁻¹ = y⁻¹ * x⁻¹`, where `x⁻¹`
denotes the left inverse `x^λ = 1 / x` (the unique element with `x^λ * x = 1`). This identity
forces left and right inverses to coincide, so the choice of inverse is immaterial. -/
def HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : Q, 1 / (x * y) = 1 / y * (1 / x)

/-- A loop is *Osborn* if it satisfies `x * ((y * z) * x) = (x^λ \ y) * (z * x)`, where
`x^λ = 1 / x` is the left inverse of `x` and `\` is left division. -/
def IsOsborn (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y z : Q, x * (y * z * x) = ldiv (1 / x) y * (z * x)

/-- A loop is *automorphic* if every inner mapping is an automorphism. -/
def IsAutomorphic (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ θ ∈ inn Q, ∀ x y : Q, θ (x * y) = θ x * θ y

/-- A loop is *torsion-free* if no element other than `1` has finite order. -/
def IsTorsionFree (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Q, (∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ x ^ k = 1) → x = 1

/-- Two loops `Q` and `Q'` are *isotopic* if there are bijections `α β γ : Q → Q'` with
`α x * β y = γ (x * y)` for all `x y : Q`. -/
def IsIsotopic (Q Q' : Type*) [Loop Q] [Loop Q'] : Prop :=
  ∃ α β γ : Q ≃ Q', ∀ x y : Q, α x * β y = γ (x * y)

/-- A loop is *universally flexible* if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible. -/
def IsUniversallyFlexible (Q : Type) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q' : Type) [Loop Q'], IsIsotopic Q Q' → IsFlexible Q'

/-- A loop is *middle Bol* if every one of its loop isotopes has the antiautomorphic inverse
property. -/
def IsMiddleBol (Q : Type) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q' : Type) [Loop Q'], IsIsotopic Q Q' → HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty Q'

/-- The *conjugacy classes* of a loop are the orbits of its inner mapping group. A loop has
*nontrivial conjugacy classes* if these orbits are not just `{1}` and `Q ∖ {1}`, i.e. some two
non-identity elements lie in different orbits of `Inn(Q)`. -/
def HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : Q, x ≠ 1 ∧ y ≠ 1 ∧ y ∉ MulAction.orbit (inn Q) x

end Loop

/-
## Subloops
-/

/-- A subloop of a loop `Q`: a subset containing `1` and closed under multiplication and both
divisions. -/
structure Subloop (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] where
  /-- The underlying set of the subloop. -/
  carrier : Set Q
  one_mem' : (1 : Q) ∈ carrier
  mul_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a * b ∈ carrier
  ldiv_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → Loop.ldiv a b ∈ carrier
  div_mem' {a b : Q} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a / b ∈ carrier

namespace Subloop

variable {Q : Type*} [Loop Q]

instance : SetLike (Subloop Q) Q where
  coe := carrier
  coe_injective' p q h := by cases p; cases q; congr

/-- The whole loop, as a subloop. -/
instance : Top (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨{ carrier := Set.univ
     one_mem' := trivial
     mul_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial
     ldiv_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial
     div_mem' := fun _ _ => trivial }⟩

/-- The trivial subloop `{1}`. -/
instance : Bot (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨{ carrier := {1}
     one_mem' := rfl
     mul_mem' := by
       rintro _ _ rfl rfl
       exact mul_one (1 : Q)
     ldiv_mem' := by
       rintro _ _ rfl rfl
       have h := Loop.mul_ldiv_cancel (1 : Q) 1
       rwa [one_mul] at h
     div_mem' := by
       rintro _ _ rfl rfl
       have h := Loop.rdiv_mul_cancel (1 : Q) 1
       rwa [mul_one] at h }⟩

/-- The intersection of a family of subloops is a subloop (the empty intersection is `⊤`). -/
instance : InfSet (Subloop Q) :=
  ⟨fun S =>
    { carrier := ⋂ T ∈ S, (T : Set Q)
      one_mem' := Set.mem_iInter₂.2 fun T _ => T.one_mem'
      mul_mem' := fun ha hb => Set.mem_iInter₂.2 fun T hT =>
        T.mul_mem' (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 ha T hT) (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 hb T hT)
      ldiv_mem' := fun ha hb => Set.mem_iInter₂.2 fun T hT =>
        T.ldiv_mem' (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 ha T hT) (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 hb T hT)
      div_mem' := fun ha hb => Set.mem_iInter₂.2 fun T hT =>
        T.div_mem' (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 ha T hT) (Set.mem_iInter₂.1 hb T hT) }⟩

/-- The subloop generated by a set. -/
def closure (s : Set Q) : Subloop Q :=
  sInf {S : Subloop Q | s ⊆ S}

/-- A subloop is itself a loop. -/
instance (S : Subloop Q) : Loop S where
  mul a b := ⟨a * b, S.mul_mem' a.2 b.2⟩
  one := ⟨1, S.one_mem'⟩
  div a b := ⟨a / b, S.div_mem' a.2 b.2⟩
  ldiv a b := ⟨Loop.ldiv a b, S.ldiv_mem' a.2 b.2⟩
  one_mul a := Subtype.ext (one_mul (a : Q))
  mul_one a := Subtype.ext (mul_one (a : Q))
  mul_ldiv_cancel a b := Subtype.ext (Loop.mul_ldiv_cancel (a : Q) b)
  ldiv_mul_cancel a b := Subtype.ext (Loop.ldiv_mul_cancel (a : Q) b)
  rdiv_mul_cancel a b := Subtype.ext (Loop.rdiv_mul_cancel (a : Q) b)
  mul_rdiv_cancel a b := Subtype.ext (Loop.mul_rdiv_cancel (a : Q) b)

/-- `N` is a *normal subloop of the subloop `H`* (Bruck): `N ≤ H` and for all `x y ∈ H`,
`x N = N x`, `x (y N) = (x y) N` and `(N x) y = N (x y)`. Equivalently, `N` is invariant under
the inner mapping group of `H`. -/
def IsNormalIn (N H : Subloop Q) : Prop :=
  N ≤ H ∧ ∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ H,
    (x * ·) '' N = (· * x) '' N ∧
    (fun n => x * (y * n)) '' N = (fun n => x * y * n) '' N ∧
    (fun n => n * x * y) '' N = (fun n => n * (x * y)) '' N

/-- `N` is a normal subloop of `Q`. -/
def IsNormal (N : Subloop Q) : Prop :=
  N.IsNormalIn ⊤

/-- `a` is *central modulo the normal subloop `N`*: its image in the quotient loop `Q / N`
commutes and associates with all elements. Here `u ∈ v N` is written `∃ n ∈ N, u = v * n`. -/
def IsCentralMod (N : Subloop Q) (a : Q) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : Q,
    (∃ n ∈ N, a * x = x * a * n) ∧
    (∃ n ∈ N, a * x * y = a * (x * y) * n) ∧
    (∃ n ∈ N, x * a * y = x * (a * y) * n) ∧
    (∃ n ∈ N, x * y * a = x * (y * a) * n)

end Subloop

namespace Loop

variable {Q : Type*} [Loop Q]

/-- A *central series* of length `n`: normal subloops `⊥ = s 0 ≤ s 1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ s n = ⊤` with
`s (i + 1) / s i` contained in the centre of `Q / s i`. -/
def IsCentralSeries {n : ℕ} (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subloop Q) : Prop :=
  s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, (s i.castSucc).IsNormal ∧ s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∀ a ∈ s i.succ, (s i.castSucc).IsCentralMod a

/-- A loop is *(centrally) nilpotent* if it has a central series. -/
def IsNilpotent (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subloop Q), IsCentralSeries s

/-- The *nilpotency class* of a nilpotent loop: the length of its shortest central series. -/
noncomputable def nilpotencyClass (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ s : Fin (n + 1) → Subloop Q, IsCentralSeries s}

/-- A loop is *solvable* if it has a subnormal series `⊥ = s 0 ≤ s 1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ s n = ⊤`, each
`s i` normal in `s (i + 1)`, whose factors `s (i + 1) / s i` are abelian groups (i.e. are
commutative and associative). -/
def IsSolvable (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subloop Q), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, (s i.castSucc).IsNormalIn (s i.succ) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ s i.succ, ∀ y ∈ s i.succ, ∀ z ∈ s i.succ,
        (∃ m ∈ s i.castSucc, x * y = y * x * m) ∧
        (∃ m ∈ s i.castSucc, x * y * z = x * (y * z) * m)

/-- A loop is *simple* if it is nontrivial and its only normal subloops are `⊥` and `⊤`. -/
def IsSimple (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  Nontrivial Q ∧ ∀ N : Subloop Q, N.IsNormal → N = ⊥ ∨ N = ⊤

/-- The *Frattini subloop* `Φ(Q)`: the intersection of all maximal (proper) subloops of `Q`.
For the trivial loop there are no maximal subloops and `Φ(Q) = Q`. -/
noncomputable def frattini (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] : Subloop Q :=
  sInf {M : Subloop Q | Maximal (· ≠ ⊤) M}

/-- `ι : Fin n → F` exhibits `F` as *the free Moufang loop on `n` generators*: `F` is Moufang
and every map from the generators to a Moufang loop `M` extends uniquely to a loop homomorphism
`F → M`. Free Moufang loops exist and are unique up to isomorphism. -/
def IsFreeMoufangLoopOn (F : Type) [Loop F] {n : ℕ} (ι : Fin n → F) : Prop :=
  IsMoufang F ∧ ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M], IsMoufang M →
    ∀ g : Fin n → M, ∃! φ : F →ₙ* M, ∀ i, φ (ι i) = g i

/-- A class `P` of finite loops is *quadratic* (Drápal) if there is a real `α > 0` such that any
two loops of order `n` in `P` defined on the same underlying set whose multiplication tables
differ in fewer than `α n ^ 2` places are isomorphic. -/
def IsQuadraticClass (P : (Q : Type) → [Loop Q] → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∀ (Q : Type) [Finite Q] (L₁ L₂ : Loop Q), @P Q L₁ → @P Q L₂ →
    (Set.ncard {p : Q × Q | L₁.mul p.1 p.2 ≠ L₂.mul p.1 p.2} : ℝ) < α * (Nat.card Q) ^ 2 →
    ∃ e : Q ≃ Q, ∀ a b : Q, e (L₁.mul a b) = L₂.mul (e a) (e b)

end Loop

/-
## Loop identities and their finite bases
-/

/-- Terms in the language of loops `(*, \, /, 1)`, with variables indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LoopTerm
  /-- A variable. -/
  | var : ℕ → LoopTerm
  /-- The constant `1`. -/
  | one : LoopTerm
  /-- Multiplication. -/
  | mul : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  /-- Left division. -/
  | ldiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm
  /-- Right division. -/
  | rdiv : LoopTerm → LoopTerm → LoopTerm

namespace LoopTerm

variable {Q : Type*} [Loop Q]

/-- Evaluate a term in a loop under an assignment of the variables. -/
def eval (v : ℕ → Q) : LoopTerm → Q
  | var i => v i
  | one => 1
  | mul s t => s.eval v * t.eval v
  | ldiv s t => Loop.ldiv (s.eval v) (t.eval v)
  | rdiv s t => s.eval v / t.eval v

end LoopTerm

namespace Loop

/-- The loop `Q` satisfies the law `l.1 = l.2`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] (l : LoopTerm × LoopTerm) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → Q, l.1.eval v = l.2.eval v

/-- A set `B` of laws is a *basis for the laws of `Q`* if the laws of `Q` are exactly the
consequences of `B`, where a law is a consequence of `B` if it holds in every loop satisfying
all the laws in `B`. -/
def IsBasisOfLaws (Q : Type) [Loop Q] (B : Set (LoopTerm × LoopTerm)) : Prop :=
  ∀ l, SatisfiesLaw Q l ↔ ∀ (R : Type) [Loop R], (∀ b ∈ B, SatisfiesLaw R b) → SatisfiesLaw R l

/-- The laws of `Q` have a finite basis. -/
def HasFiniteBasisOfLaws (Q : Type) [Loop Q] : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Set (LoopTerm × LoopTerm), B.Finite ∧ IsBasisOfLaws Q B

end Loop

/-- A (not necessarily associative) algebra is *alternative* if it satisfies
`(x * x) * y = x * (x * y)` and `(y * x) * x = y * (x * x)`. -/
def IsAlternative (A : Type*) [Mul A] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : A, x * x * y = x * (x * y) ∧ y * x * x = y * (x * x)

/-
## Basic checks of the definitions
-/

/-- Every group is a loop, with `ldiv a b = a⁻¹ * b` and `b / a = b * a⁻¹`. -/
def Loop.ofGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Loop G where
  ldiv a b := a⁻¹ * b
  mul_ldiv_cancel a b := by simp
  ldiv_mul_cancel a b := by simp
  rdiv_mul_cancel a b := by simp
  mul_rdiv_cancel a b := by simp

/-- Groups are associative loops. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.ofGroup_associative (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup G; Std.Associative (α := G) (· * ·) :=
  ⟨mul_assoc⟩

/-- Groups are Moufang loops. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.ofGroup_isMoufang (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup G; Loop.IsMoufang G := by
  intro x y z
  simp [mul_assoc]

/-- Groups are left Bol loops. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.ofGroup_isLeftBol (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup G; Loop.IsLeftBol G := by
  intro x y z
  simp [mul_assoc]

/-- Groups are Osborn loops. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.ofGroup_isOsborn (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup G; Loop.IsOsborn G := by
  intro x y z
  simp [Loop.ofGroup, mul_assoc]

/-- Groups have the antiautomorphic inverse property. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.ofGroup_hasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    letI := Loop.ofGroup G; Loop.HasAntiautomorphicInverseProperty G := by
  intro x y
  simp [mul_inv_rev]

/-- In a loop, `x ^ 3 = ((1 * x) * x) * x`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem Loop.pow_three (Q : Type*) [Loop Q] (x : Q) : x ^ 3 = 1 * x * x * x :=
  rfl

/-
## The problems
-/

open Loop

/--
**Abelian by cyclic groups resulting in Moufang loops, part (i).**
Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal subloop $M$ which is an abelian group (i.e. $M$ is
associative and commutative) of odd order, such that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger
than $3$. Is $L$ a group?

Here "$L/M$ is a cyclic group of order $> 3$" is expressed as the existence of a surjective loop
homomorphism $f \colon L \to C$ onto a cyclic group $C$ with $|C| > 3$ and kernel $M$; "of odd
order" includes finiteness of $M$; and "$L$ is a group" as $L$ being associative. The bound
$3$ is sharp: there is a commutative Moufang loop of order $81$ with a normal commutative
subgroup of order $27$. Proposed by Michael Kinyon, based on Chein and Rajah (2000).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L → ∀ M : Subloop L, M.IsNormal →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, ∀ c ∈ M, a * b * c = a * (b * c)) →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, a * b = b * a) → Odd (Nat.card M) →
      (∃ (C : Type) (_ : Group C) (_ : IsCyclic C) (f : L →ₙ* C),
        Function.Surjective f ∧ (∀ x, f x = 1 ↔ x ∈ M) ∧ 3 < Nat.card C) →
      Std.Associative (α := L) (· * ·) := by
  sorry

/--
**Abelian by cyclic groups resulting in Moufang loops, part (ii).**
Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal subloop $M$ which is an abelian group of odd order, such
that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger than $3$. If moreover the orders of $M$ and $L/M$
are relatively prime, is $L$ a group?

This is the special case of part (i) with the extra hypothesis $\gcd(|M|, |L/M|) = 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i.variants.coprime :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L → ∀ M : Subloop L, M.IsNormal →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, ∀ c ∈ M, a * b * c = a * (b * c)) →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, a * b = b * a) → Odd (Nat.card M) →
      (∃ (C : Type) (_ : Group C) (_ : IsCyclic C) (f : L →ₙ* C),
        Function.Surjective f ∧ (∀ x, f x = 1 ↔ x ∈ M) ∧ 3 < Nat.card C ∧
          Nat.Coprime (Nat.card M) (Nat.card C)) →
      Std.Associative (α := L) (· * ·) := by
  sorry

/--
**Embedding CMLs of period 3 into alternative algebras.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '03): any finite commutative Moufang loop of period $3$ (i.e. of
exponent $3$: $x^3 = 1$ for all $x$) can be embedded into a commutative alternative algebra.

The algebra is taken to be a unital commutative alternative algebra $A$ over some field $F$ (only
characteristic $3$ is possible when the loop is not associative), and "embedded" means that there
is an injective map $L \to A$ preserving multiplication and $1$; its image then consists of
invertible elements of $A$. Grishkov and Shestakov (2011) proved this for the free commutative
Moufang loop of exponent $3$ on fewer than $7$ generators.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ii
    (L : Type) [Loop L] [Finite L] (hL : IsMoufang L) (hcomm : ∀ x y : L, x * y = y * x)
    (hexp : ∀ x : L, x ^ 3 = 1) :
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (A : Type) (_ : NonAssocRing A) (_ : Module F A)
      (_ : IsScalarTower F A A) (_ : SMulCommClass F A A),
      (∀ a b : A, a * b = b * a) ∧ IsAlternative A ∧ ∃ φ : L →* A, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/--
**Frattini subloop for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '11): let $L$ be a finite Moufang loop and $\Phi(L)$ the intersection
of all maximal subloops of $L$. Then $\Phi(L)$ is a normal nilpotent subloop of $L$.

Nilpotency means central nilpotency of the loop $\Phi(L)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iii
    (L : Type) [Loop L] [Finite L] (hL : IsMoufang L) :
    (frattini L).IsNormal ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent (frattini L) := by
  sorry

/--
**The restricted Burnside problem for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '11): let $M$ be a finite Moufang loop of exponent $n$ with $m$
generators. Then there exists a function $f(n, m)$ such that $|M| < f(n, m)$.

That is, $f(n, m)$ depends only on $n$ and $m$: for every $n \geq 1$ and $m$ there are only
finitely many finite $m$-generated Moufang loops of exponent $n$ up to isomorphism. The case of
prime exponent is known (Grishkov for $p \neq 3$, Bruck for commutative loops and $p = 3$, Nagy
for $p = 3$), as is the case $n = p^k$ with $p \neq 2, 3$ (Grishkov, Sabinina and Zelmanov).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iv :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ n m : ℕ, 0 < n → ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M] [Finite M], IsMoufang M →
      (∀ x : M, x ^ n = 1) → (∃ g : Fin m → M, Subloop.closure (Set.range g) = ⊤) →
      Nat.card M < f n m := by
  sorry

/--
**The Sanov and M. Hall theorems for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '11): let $L$ be a finitely generated Moufang loop of exponent $4$
or $6$ (i.e. $x^4 = 1$ for all $x$, or $x^6 = 1$ for all $x$). Then $L$ is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.v
    (L : Type) [Loop L] (hL : IsMoufang L) (hfg : ∃ s : Finset L, Subloop.closure (s : Set L) = ⊤)
    (hexp : (∀ x : L, x ^ 4 = 1) ∨ (∀ x : L, x ^ 6 = 1)) :
    Finite L := by
  sorry

/--
**Torsion in free Moufang loops.**
Let $MF_n$ be the free Moufang loop with $n$ generators.
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '03): $MF_3$ is torsion free but $MF_n$ with $n > 4$ is not.

Free Moufang loops are characterised here by their universal property
(`Loop.IsFreeMoufangLoopOn`); nothing is claimed about $n = 4$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vi :
    (∀ (F : Type) [Loop F] (ι : Fin 3 → F), IsFreeMoufangLoopOn F ι → IsTorsionFree F) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, 4 < n → ∀ (F : Type) [Loop F] (ι : Fin n → F), IsFreeMoufangLoopOn F ι →
      ¬ IsTorsionFree F := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Moufang loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
Let $(Q, *)$, $(Q, +)$ be two quasigroups on the same underlying set $Q$; their distance
$d(*, +)$ is the number of pairs $(a, b)$ with $a * b \neq a + b$. A class of finite quasigroups
is quadratic if there is a real $\alpha > 0$ such that any two quasigroups of order $n$ from the
class with $d(*, +) < \alpha n^2$ are isomorphic. Are Moufang loops quadratic?

Drápal proved that groups are quadratic with $\alpha = 1/9$ and $2$-groups with $\alpha = 1/4$.
Proposed by Aleš Drápal at Loops '99.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q _ => IsMoufang Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Bol loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
With the notion of a quadratic class of finite quasigroups as in part (vii): are (left) Bol loops
quadratic? Since Moufang loops are Bol loops, a positive answer implies a positive answer to part
(vii). Proposed by Aleš Drápal at Loops '99.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii.variants.bol :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q _ => IsLeftBol Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Universally flexible loop that is not middle Bol.**
A loop is universally flexible if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible, i.e. satisfies
$(xy)x = x(yx)$. A loop is middle Bol if every one of its loop isotopes has the antiautomorphic
inverse property $(xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1}$. Is there a finite, universally flexible loop that is
not middle Bol? Proposed by Michael Kinyon at Loops '03.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.viii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsUniversallyFlexible Q ∧
      ¬ IsMiddleBol Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes.**
Is there a finite simple nonassociative (left) Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes?

The conjugacy classes of a loop $Q$ are the orbits of its inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$
(Johnson and Smith); they are nontrivial if they are not just $\{1\}$ and $Q \setminus \{1\}$.
Proposed by Kenneth W. Johnson and Jonathan D. H. Smith at the 2nd Mile High Conference, 2009.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ix :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧
      ¬ Std.Associative (α := Q) (· * ·) ∧ IsLeftBol Q ∧ HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ is nilpotent. Is $Q$ (centrally)
nilpotent?

The answer is affirmative if $Q$ is finite (Niemenmaa 2009); the general case is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], Group.IsNilpotent (inn Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture, solvable version.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ is nilpotent. Is $Q$ solvable?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x.variants.solvable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], Group.IsNilpotent (inn Q) → Loop.IsSolvable Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$. Is $Q$ (centrally)
nilpotent?

When $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ is finite and abelian, $Q$ is nilpotent (Niemenmaa and Kepka), so the
question is open only in the infinite case. Proposed at Loops '07.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsMulCommutative (inn Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group: bounded nilpotency class.**
If every loop with abelian inner mapping group is nilpotent, is there a bound on the nilpotency
class of such loops? That is, is there a $c$ such that every nilpotent loop $Q$ with abelian
$\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ has nilpotency class at most $c$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.bounded_class :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsMulCommutative (inn Q) →
      Loop.IsNilpotent Q → nilpotencyClass Q ≤ c := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group: nilpotency class higher than 3.**
Can the nilpotency class of a (nilpotent) loop $Q$ with abelian inner mapping group be higher
than $3$?

Loops of Csörgő type (nilpotent of class at least $3$ with abelian inner mapping group) exist,
but none of class higher than $3$ is known.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.class_gt_three :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), IsMulCommutative (inn Q) ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      3 < nilpotencyClass Q := by
  sorry

/--
**A finite nilpotent loop without a finite basis for its laws.**
Does there exist a finite (centrally) nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws? (Posed
by M. R. Vaughan-Lee in the Kourovka Notebook as "construct a finite nilpotent loop with no
finite basis for its laws".)

Laws are identities in the language $(\cdot, \backslash, /, 1)$ of loops; a set $B$ of laws is a
basis for the laws of $Q$ if the laws of $Q$ are exactly the laws holding in every loop that
satisfies $B$. There is a finite loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee, 1979), but
it is not nilpotent.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      ¬ HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple nonassociative automorphic loop.**
Does there exist a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop? (A loop is automorphic if all
its inner mappings are automorphisms.)

Such a loop cannot be commutative (Grishkov, Kinyon and Nagy, 2013) nor have odd order (Kinyon,
Kunen, Phillips and Vojtěchovský, 2013). Proposed by Michael Kinyon at Loops '03.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧ IsAutomorphic Q ∧
      ¬ Std.Associative (α := Q) (· * ·) := by
  sorry

/--
**Universality of Osborn loops.**
A loop is Osborn if it satisfies the identity $x((yz)x) = (x^\lambda \backslash y)(zx)$, where
$x^\lambda$ is the left inverse of $x$. Is every Osborn loop universal, that is, is every loop
isotope of an Osborn loop Osborn? Proposed by Michael Kinyon at the Mile High conference, 2005.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiv :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsOsborn Q →
      ∀ (Q' : Type) [Loop Q'], IsIsotopic Q Q' → IsOsborn Q' := by
  sorry

end ProblemsInLoopTheoryAndQuasigroupTheory
attempts.decomposition_objections: None substantive. Two remarks: (1) slot i's note reads "L/M cyclic of (finite) order > 3"; the article's wording does not exclude an infinite cyclic quotient, but I followed the table (finite, via `3 < Nat.card C`). (2) For slots vii.variants.bol and ix the article's "Bol loop" is one-sided; I use left Bol throughout — by passing to the opposite loop the left- and right-Bol versions of these questions are equivalent (isomorphism, simplicity, associativity, finiteness, Inn(Q) and table distance are all preserved), so no content is lost.
modeling_decisions: Mathlib and the repo have no loops/quasigroups, so the file defines a class `Loop` equationally (mul, 1, left division `ldiv`, right division `/` with the four cancellation laws) and all loop-theoretic notions on top of it. Powers `x ^ n` are right-associated (`npowRec`); they are only used for Moufang loops, which are diassociative, so the bracketing is immaterial.

Normality of a subloop is Bruck's definition via coset equalities xN = Nx, x(yN) = (xy)N, (Nx)y = N(xy) (equivalently Inn-invariance); `Subloop.IsNormalIn N H` gives normality inside a subloop H, used for subnormal series.

Quotient loops are never constructed. 'L/M is a cyclic group of order > 3' (slots i, i.coprime) is encoded as a surjective `MulHom` f : L →ₙ* C onto a cyclic group C with |C| > 3 and kernel M (a MulHom between loops automatically preserves 1 and divisions, and L/ker f ≅ C). Central and abelian-factor conditions are phrased through coset membership u ∈ vN as ∃ n ∈ N, u = v * n, which is valid because N is normal (in Q, resp. in the next term).

Central nilpotency = existence of a central series of normal subloops ⊥ = s 0 ≤ … ≤ s n = ⊤ with s(i+1) central modulo s i (Bruck); `nilpotencyClass` = shortest such length (equals the upper-central-series length). Solvability is classical loop solvability: a subnormal series with each term normal in the next and factors that are abelian groups (commutative and associative), not congruence solvability.

Slot i: 'M abelian subgroup of odd order' = M associative and commutative on its elements with `Odd (Nat.card M)` (which forces M finite); 'L is a group' = `Std.Associative` of the loop multiplication. The `M.IsNormal` hypothesis is kept to mirror the text although being a kernel already implies it. Slot i.coprime adds `Nat.Coprime (Nat.card M) (Nat.card C)` inside the existential over C.

Slot ii: 'commutative alternative algebra' = a unital nonassociative ring A (`NonAssocRing`) that is commutative and alternative, with a module structure over an existentially quantified field F using Mathlib's nonassociative-algebra encoding `[Module F A] [IsScalarTower F A A] [SMulCommClass F A A]`; 'embedded' = an injective `MonoidHom` L →* A (multiplicative, 1 ↦ 1); the image then consists of invertible elements. No characteristic restriction is imposed (for nonassociative L only char 3 is possible anyway, and the associative case is trivial in both readings). The notes' '1 + x' (nil-ideal) reading would be a stronger conjecture; I chose the literal reading.

Slot iii: maximal subloop = `Maximal (· ≠ ⊤)` in the SetLike order on `Subloop`; Φ(L) = sInf over these (sInf ∅ = ⊤ for the trivial loop). 'Nilpotent subloop' is central nilpotency of Φ(L) as a loop in its own right (subtype instance).

Slot iv: stated as ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ n m, 0 < n → (every finite m-generated Moufang loop of exponent n has Nat.card < f n m); 'm generators' = a generating family `Fin m → M` under `Subloop.closure`. `0 < n` is needed since exponent 0 would be vacuous.

Slot vi: the free Moufang loop is characterised by its universal property `IsFreeMoufangLoopOn` (Moufang, and every map of generators into a Moufang loop in `Type` extends uniquely to a `MulHom`), and the statement quantifies over all F satisfying it. This is faithful because free Moufang loops exist and are unique up to isomorphism, but a reviewer should note the statement relies on that external existence fact to be non-vacuous. Torsion-free = no element ≠ 1 with x ^ k = 1 for some k > 0; n = 4 is not covered.

Slots vii/vii.bol: `IsQuadraticClass P` takes a predicate on loop structures and quantifies over two `Loop` structures L₁ L₂ on the same finite type; distance = `Set.ncard` of pairs where the multiplications differ; the bound is strict `< α * n^2` with α : ℝ, 0 < α uniform over all n; isomorphism = a bijection e with e (a *₁ b) = e a *₂ e b. The class is restricted to loops (the article defines quadraticity for quasigroups), which is harmless since Moufang/Bol loops are loops.

Slot viii: loop isotopy is the general notion (bijections α β γ : Q ≃ Q' with α x * β y = γ (x * y), Q' any loop in `Type`), not principal isotopes. The antiautomorphic inverse property is stated with left inverses x^λ = 1 / x as 1 / (x*y) = (1/y) * (1/x); this identity forces two-sided inverses, so the choice of inverse is immaterial.

Slot ix: 'conjugacy classes' = orbits of Inn(Q) = Mlt(Q) ⊓ stabilizer of 1 in Perm Q (Mlt = closure of left and right translations); 'nontrivial' = some two non-identity elements lie in different Inn(Q)-orbits (i.e. the classes are not just {1} and Q∖{1}), as fixed by the notes. Simplicity includes `Nontrivial Q` (as in Mathlib's `IsSimpleGroup`); irrelevant here since nonassociativity forces nontriviality.
Slots x, x.solvable, xi: Inn(Q) nilpotent/abelian via Mathlib's `Group.IsNilpotent` / `IsMulCommutative` on the subgroup ↥(inn Q); loops are arbitrary (possibly infinite) types in `Type`.

Slot xi.bounded_class: the 'if so' is handled by restricting to nilpotent Q: ∃ c, ∀ Q with abelian Inn(Q) and nilpotent, nilpotencyClass Q ≤ c. Slot xi.class_gt_three: ∃ nilpotent Q with abelian Inn(Q) and 3 < nilpotencyClass Q.

Slot xii: laws are pairs of terms of a bespoke inductive `LoopTerm` in the signature (·, \, /, 1) with ℕ-indexed variables; Q satisfies a law if it holds under every assignment; B is a basis for the laws of Q if the laws of Q are exactly the laws holding in every loop (in `Type`) satisfying B (semantic consequence, which equals equational derivability by Birkhoff's completeness theorem); 'construct' is read as the existence question, per the notes.

Slot xiii: automorphic = every θ ∈ Inn(Q) is multiplicative. Slot xiv: Osborn identity x((yz)x) = (x^λ \ y)(zx) with x^λ = 1 / x and \ = `ldiv`; universality = every loop isotope (general isotopy, any loop Q' in `Type`) is Osborn.
All problem statements quantify over types in `Type` (universe 0), following the repository's style (e.g. BoundedBurnsideProblem).

statement_blocks.problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_t:
/--
**Abelian by cyclic groups resulting in Moufang loops, part (i).**
Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal subloop $M$ which is an abelian group (i.e. $M$ is
associative and commutative) of odd order, such that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger
than $3$. Is $L$ a group?

Here "$L/M$ is a cyclic group of order $> 3$" is expressed as the existence of a surjective loop
homomorphism $f \colon L \to C$ onto a cyclic group $C$ with $|C| > 3$ and kernel $M$; "of odd
order" includes finiteness of $M$; and "$L$ is a group" as $L$ being associative. The bound
$3$ is sharp: there is a commutative Moufang loop of order $81$ with a normal commutative
subgroup of order $27$. Proposed by Michael Kinyon, based on Chein and Rajah (2000).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L → ∀ M : Subloop L, M.IsNormal →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, ∀ c ∈ M, a * b * c = a * (b * c)) →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, a * b = b * a) → Odd (Nat.card M) →
      (∃ (C : Type) (_ : Group C) (_ : IsCyclic C) (f : L →ₙ* C),
        Function.Surjective f ∧ (∀ x, f x = 1 ↔ x ∈ M) ∧ 3 < Nat.card C) →
      Std.Associative (α := L) (· * ·) := by
  sorry

/--
**Abelian by cyclic groups resulting in Moufang loops, part (ii).**
Let $L$ be a Moufang loop with a normal subloop $M$ which is an abelian group of odd order, such
that $L/M$ is a cyclic group of order bigger than $3$. If moreover the orders of $M$ and $L/M$
are relatively prime, is $L$ a group?

This is the special case of part (i) with the extra hypothesis $\gcd(|M|, |L/M|) = 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.i.variants.coprime :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Type) [Loop L], IsMoufang L → ∀ M : Subloop L, M.IsNormal →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, ∀ c ∈ M, a * b * c = a * (b * c)) →
      (∀ a ∈ M, ∀ b ∈ M, a * b = b * a) → Odd (Nat.card M) →
      (∃ (C : Type) (_ : Group C) (_ : IsCyclic C) (f : L →ₙ* C),
        Function.Surjective f ∧ (∀ x, f x = 1 ↔ x ∈ M) ∧ 3 < Nat.card C ∧
          Nat.Coprime (Nat.card M) (Nat.card C)) →
      Std.Associative (α := L) (· * ·) := by
  sorry

/--
**Embedding CMLs of period 3 into alternative algebras.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '03): any finite commutative Moufang loop of period $3$ (i.e. of
exponent $3$: $x^3 = 1$ for all $x$) can be embedded into a commutative alternative algebra.

The algebra is taken to be a unital commutative alternative algebra $A$ over some field $F$ (only
characteristic $3$ is possible when the loop is not associative), and "embedded" means that there
is an injective map $L \to A$ preserving multiplication and $1$; its image then consists of
invertible elements of $A$. Grishkov and Shestakov (2011) proved this for the free commutative
Moufang loop of exponent $3$ on fewer than $7$ generators.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 17 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ii
    (L : Type) [Loop L] [Finite L] (hL : IsMoufang L) (hcomm : ∀ x y : L, x * y = y * x)
    (hexp : ∀ x : L, x ^ 3 = 1) :
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (A : Type) (_ : NonAssocRing A) (_ : Module F A)
      (_ : IsScalarTower F A A) (_ : SMulCommClass F A A),
      (∀ a b : A, a * b = b * a) ∧ IsAlternative A ∧ ∃ φ : L →* A, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

/--
**Frattini subloop for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '11): let $L$ be a finite Moufang loop and $\Phi(L)$ the intersection
of all maximal subloops of $L$. Then $\Phi(L)$ is a normal nilpotent subloop of $L$.

Nilpotency means central nilpotency of the loop $\Phi(L)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iii
    (L : Type) [Loop L] [Finite L] (hL : IsMoufang L) :
    (frattini L).IsNormal ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent (frattini L) := by
  sorry

/--
**The restricted Burnside problem for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '11): let $M$ be a finite Moufang loop of exponent $n$ with $m$
generators. Then there exists a function $f(n, m)$ such that $|M| < f(n, m)$.

That is, $f(n, m)$ depends only on $n$ and $m$: for every $n \geq 1$ and $m$ there are only
finitely many finite $m$-generated Moufang loops of exponent $n$ up to isomorphism. The case of
prime exponent is known (Grishkov for $p \neq 3$, Bruck for commutative loops and $p = 3$, Nagy
for $p = 3$), as is the case $n = p^k$ with $p \neq 2, 3$ (Grishkov, Sabinina and Zelmanov).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.iv :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ, ∀ n m : ℕ, 0 < n → ∀ (M : Type) [Loop M] [Finite M], IsMoufang M →
      (∀ x : M, x ^ n = 1) → (∃ g : Fin m → M, Subloop.closure (Set.range g) = ⊤) →
      Nat.card M < f n m := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes.**
Is there a finite simple nonassociative (left) Bol loop with nontrivial conjugacy classes?

The conjugacy classes of a loop $Q$ are the orbits of its inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$
(Johnson and Smith); they are nontrivial if they are not just $\{1\}$ and $Q \setminus \{1\}$.
Proposed by Kenneth W. Johnson and Jonathan D. H. Smith at the 2nd Mile High Conference, 2009.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.ix :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧
      ¬ Std.Associative (α := Q) (· * ·) ∧ IsLeftBol Q ∧ HasNontrivialConjugacyClasses Q := by
  sorry

/--
**The Sanov and M. Hall theorems for Moufang loops.**
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '11): let $L$ be a finitely generated Moufang loop of exponent $4$
or $6$ (i.e. $x^4 = 1$ for all $x$, or $x^6 = 1$ for all $x$). Then $L$ is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.v
    (L : Type) [Loop L] (hL : IsMoufang L) (hfg : ∃ s : Finset L, Subloop.closure (s : Set L) = ⊤)
    (hexp : (∀ x : L, x ^ 4 = 1) ∨ (∀ x : L, x ^ 6 = 1)) :
    Finite L := by
  sorry

/--
**Torsion in free Moufang loops.**
Let $MF_n$ be the free Moufang loop with $n$ generators.
Conjecture (Grishkov, Loops '03): $MF_3$ is torsion free but $MF_n$ with $n > 4$ is not.

Free Moufang loops are characterised here by their universal property
(`Loop.IsFreeMoufangLoopOn`); nothing is claimed about $n = 4$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vi :
    (∀ (F : Type) [Loop F] (ι : Fin 3 → F), IsFreeMoufangLoopOn F ι → IsTorsionFree F) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, 4 < n → ∀ (F : Type) [Loop F] (ι : Fin n → F), IsFreeMoufangLoopOn F ι →
      ¬ IsTorsionFree F := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Moufang loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
Let $(Q, *)$, $(Q, +)$ be two quasigroups on the same underlying set $Q$; their distance
$d(*, +)$ is the number of pairs $(a, b)$ with $a * b \neq a + b$. A class of finite quasigroups
is quadratic if there is a real $\alpha > 0$ such that any two quasigroups of order $n$ from the
class with $d(*, +) < \alpha n^2$ are isomorphic. Are Moufang loops quadratic?

Drápal proved that groups are quadratic with $\alpha = 1/9$ and $2$-groups with $\alpha = 1/4$.
Proposed by Aleš Drápal at Loops '99.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q _ => IsMoufang Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Are two Bol loops with similar multiplication tables isomorphic?**
With the notion of a quadratic class of finite quasigroups as in part (vii): are (left) Bol loops
quadratic? Since Moufang loops are Bol loops, a positive answer implies a positive answer to part
(vii). Proposed by Aleš Drápal at Loops '99.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.vii.variants.bol :
    answer(sorry) ↔ IsQuadraticClass fun Q _ => IsLeftBol Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Universally flexible loop that is not middle Bol.**
A loop is universally flexible if every one of its loop isotopes is flexible, i.e. satisfies
$(xy)x = x(yx)$. A loop is middle Bol if every one of its loop isotopes has the antiautomorphic
inverse property $(xy)^{-1} = y^{-1}x^{-1}$. Is there a finite, universally flexible loop that is
not middle Bol? Proposed by Michael Kinyon at Loops '03.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.viii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsUniversallyFlexible Q ∧
      ¬ IsMiddleBol Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ is nilpotent. Is $Q$ (centrally)
nilpotent?

The answer is affirmative if $Q$ is finite (Niemenmaa 2009); the general case is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], Group.IsNilpotent (inn Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Niemenmaa's conjecture, solvable version.**
Let $Q$ be a loop whose inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ is nilpotent. Is $Q$ solvable?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.x.variants.solvable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], Group.IsNilpotent (inn Q) → Loop.IsSolvable Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group.**
Let $Q$ be a loop with abelian inner mapping group $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$. Is $Q$ (centrally)
nilpotent?

When $\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ is finite and abelian, $Q$ is nilpotent (Niemenmaa and Kepka), so the
question is open only in the infinite case. Proposed at Loops '07.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsMulCommutative (inn Q) → Loop.IsNilpotent Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group: bounded nilpotency class.**
If every loop with abelian inner mapping group is nilpotent, is there a bound on the nilpotency
class of such loops? That is, is there a $c$ such that every nilpotent loop $Q$ with abelian
$\mathrm{Inn}(Q)$ has nilpotency class at most $c$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.bounded_class :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsMulCommutative (inn Q) →
      Loop.IsNilpotent Q → nilpotencyClass Q ≤ c := by
  sorry

/--
**Loops with abelian inner mapping group: nilpotency class higher than 3.**
Can the nilpotency class of a (nilpotent) loop $Q$ with abelian inner mapping group be higher
than $3$?

Loops of Csörgő type (nilpotent of class at least $3$ with abelian inner mapping group) exist,
but none of class higher than $3$ is known.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xi.variants.class_gt_three :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), IsMulCommutative (inn Q) ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      3 < nilpotencyClass Q := by
  sorry

/--
**A finite nilpotent loop without a finite basis for its laws.**
Does there exist a finite (centrally) nilpotent loop with no finite basis for its laws? (Posed
by M. R. Vaughan-Lee in the Kourovka Notebook as "construct a finite nilpotent loop with no
finite basis for its laws".)

Laws are identities in the language $(\cdot, \backslash, /, 1)$ of loops; a set $B$ of laws is a
basis for the laws of $Q$ if the laws of $Q$ are exactly the laws holding in every loop that
satisfies $B$. There is a finite loop with no finite basis for its laws (Vaughan-Lee, 1979), but
it is not nilpotent.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ Loop.IsNilpotent Q ∧
      ¬ HasFiniteBasisOfLaws Q := by
  sorry

/--
**Finite simple nonassociative automorphic loop.**
Does there exist a nonassociative finite simple automorphic loop? (A loop is automorphic if all
its inner mappings are automorphisms.)

Such a loop cannot be commutative (Grishkov, Kinyon and Nagy, 2013) nor have odd order (Kinyon,
Kunen, Phillips and Vojtěchovský, 2013). Proposed by Michael Kinyon at Loops '03.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Loop Q), Finite Q ∧ IsSimple Q ∧ IsAutomorphic Q ∧
      ¬ Std.Associative (α := Q) (· * ·) := by
  sorry

/--
**Universality of Osborn loops.**
A loop is Osborn if it satisfies the identity $x((yz)x) = (x^\lambda \backslash y)(zx)$, where
$x^\lambda$ is the left inverse of $x$. Is every Osborn loop universal, that is, is every loop
isotope of an Osborn loop Osborn? Proposed by Michael Kinyon at the Mile High conference, 2005.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem problems_in_loop_theory_and_quasigroup_theory.parts.xiv :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (Q : Type) [Loop Q], IsOsborn Q →
      ∀ (Q' : Type) [Loop Q'], IsIsotopic Q Q' → IsOsborn Q' := by
  sorry
